osaka_sushi_hamuro.vegan_detail: Not vegan: a sushi and seafood counter.
osaka_sushi_hamuro.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 17:00–23:00 (L.O. 22:30); closed Sundays, open holidays, plus irregular days (Tabelog). Hard to reserve (January 2026). Cards accepted (Tabelog).
osaka_sushi_hamuro.notes: [Sushi · a six-seat alley counter off Shinsaibashi-suji] A six-seat sushi counter at the end of a narrow alley, where only the sign shows from the street. It's been open since 2015, and the owner has thirty years of experience. The meal is an omakase of seasonal fish, sushi and small dishes, and you can add favorites. Diners remember the kohada (one called it the best ever), sweet red sea urchin, nodoguro, katsuo tataki, crab, and winter fugu milt. It finishes with ushiojiru. The chef pairs sake to the food. The owner is gentle and the room calm, and regulars keep it full; reservations are hard to get. Courses are good value, drinks less so. Reviewers spent about ¥10,000–30,000.

chef_bio.background: Owner with 30 years of experience (April 2024 review).

anecdotes.text: "The crab, nodoguro (blackthroat sea perch), and katsuo (skipjack tuna) tataki were incredible… The kohada (gizzard shad) was the best I've ever had." — September 2024.
"The owner has a gentle demeanor, making it a comfortable place to enjoy a leisurely meal. I ordered the omakase and added a few of my favorite dishes." — December 2025.

osaka_misono_hozenji.gf_detail: Not gluten-free in practice: kara-age, simmered and sauced dishes.
osaka_misono_hozenji.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 17:00–22:30 (L.O. 22:00); closed Sunday (Tabelog). Reserve: fills within minutes (December 2025). Cards accepted; no e-money or QR (Tabelog).
osaka_misono_hozenji.notes: [Japanese · a chicken specialist beside Hōzenji] A chicken restaurant in the building next to Mizukake Fudō, cooking domestically raised young chickens from sashimi to rice. The assorted chicken sashimi is fresh and bouncy, the thigh tataki hits hard with garlic, and the kara-age, especially the crisp wings, is a favorite; one diner ordered four plates of grilled cartilage. Look also for fried chicken skin rolled with green onion, liver, gizzards and a spicy simmered chicken skin to eat over rice. Courses run to mizutaki, refined in chicken flavor, with rice porridge, and there is a dry curry omurice. Service is quiet but kind, with plates split for groups. Seats fill within minutes, so reserve. Sake is limited; beer and shochu are there.

chef_bio.background: Chicken specialist using domestically raised young chickens; official site tori-misono.com (Tabelog).

anecdotes.text: "The sashimi was fresh and had a nice bounce. The kara-age was juicy with a strong meaty flavor… The tataki was robust with a great garlic kick." — October 2025.
"We started with chicken breast and wings, followed by a delicious mizutaki (chicken hot pot). The refined flavor of the chicken in the mizutaki was outstanding." — March 2026, course.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 公式 tori-misono.com。食べログ(店舗会員): みその、大阪市中央区難波1-2-10 法善寺MEOUTOビル1F、法善寺水掛不動尊の隣のビル、月〜土17:00〜22:30(L.O.22:00)、日曜休み、カード可、電子マネー・QR不可、国産の若鶏を使った鶏料理の専門店。口コミ(2025年2月〜2026年3月): 誕生日にコース、刺身・手羽先・ドライカレー、カウンターと座敷、なんこつ唐揚げ、鶏刺し、手羽先唐揚げ、レバー焼き、ドライカレーオムライス、サラダ、レバー煮、鶏皮、チゲ、日本酒の種類は少なめ、焼酎、奥の個室のテーブル、刺身は新鮮で弾力、ジューシーな唐揚げ、にんにくの効いたたたき、ねぎを巻いた鶏皮揚げ、取り分けてくれる、ピリ辛の鶏皮煮とご飯、焼きなんこつ4皿、予約なしで入れたがすぐ満席、刺身の盛り合わせ、砂肝、口数は少ないが親切、コースの水炊きと雑炊。

osaka_yakitori_jin_souemoncho.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 18:00–3:00 am; closed Sunday (Tabelog). Six counter seats; call ahead (2016 review). Cash only: no cards or e-money (Tabelog). Smoking allowed (Tabelog).
osaka_yakitori_jin_souemoncho.notes: [Yakitori · a six-seat back-alley counter in Souemoncho] A tiny yakitori counter so deep in a Souemoncho back alley that one diner would never have found it unaided. The current owner took over in January 2014 and kept the name. Skewers are generous and thick: bonjiri, skin, negima, tsukune and yagen nankotsu are favorites. The house draw for some is the chicken liver sashimi, cooked at low temperature. Also on the board: thigh tataki, gizzard, red sausage, a spicy yam kimchi, smashed cucumber, and a chazuke in chicken broth to finish. It's a proper old-school local joint. One diner waited a while for orders. Only six seats, so call ahead. Open until 3 am; closed Sundays. Cash only.

chef_bio.origin: Current owner took over 11 January 2014, keeping the name (Tabelog)
chef_bio.background: Back-alley yakitori counter (Tabelog, staff-maintained).

anecdotes.text: "When I think of Jin, I can't help but crave… liver sashimi! It's cooked at a low temperature, and the texture is so amazing that I always want more!" — September 2023.
"The interior is cozy, with about five counter seats, making it easy to connect with the chef." — October 2026.

osaka_isshin_hozenji.notes: [Sushi · a ten-seat counter by Hōzenji's Mizukake Fudō] A long-established sushi counter in the Hōzenji lanes, close to Mizukake Fudō, with ten seats and the calm air of a long-established shop. The head chef is particular about fish, and once turned away a red clam that wasn't fresh enough. Blue crab is a long-running highlight. A July 2026 dinner ran from sashimi and rock oysters to uzaku, an abalone gunkan and tekka maki, with Kamo Tsuru Gold sake, which carries petal-shaped gold leaf. Stories of the shop's history come with the meal. It is pricey: reviewers spent ¥15,000–30,000, and one walk-in felt the bill outran the value. Closed Mondays.

chef_bio.background: Sushi counter in Hōzenji (Tabelog, staff-maintained).

anecdotes.text: "I actually wanted to order my favorite red clam, but it was deemed not fresh enough upon opening, so I couldn't have it… This time, the standout ingredient was the blue crab." — February 2024.
"We also enjoyed a unique Japanese sake, Kamo Tsuru Gold, which features cherry blossom petal-shaped pure gold leaf." — July 2026.

osaka_yakiniku_p_takanosuke.gf_detail: Not gluten-free in practice: marinated meats and yukhoe sauce; miso with the senmai.
osaka_yakiniku_p_takanosuke.hours_raw: Daily 18:00–2:00 am; closing days may vary (Tabelog); one diner noted 3 am (February 2025). Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog). Smoking allowed (Tabelog).
osaka_yakiniku_p_takanosuke.notes: [Yakiniku · a six-seat alley counter where the master grills] A hidden yakiniku counter in a narrow Souemoncho alley, next door to Hiromiya. There are no grills at the seats: the master grills each cut and serves it at its best, so up to about seven diners squeeze in close. Portions are about half the usual size, so you can try many cuts. Start with white senmai, when there is any, with sesame oil, salt and a moreish miso. Then go to aburi yukke, wagyu tataki, salted tongue, outside skirt and kalbi. A Korean-style cold tofu with kimchi and seaweed is a side. It's easy to drop by alone, and the owner suits the room. Open late, to 2 am. Cash only; smoking allowed.

chef_bio.background: Counter yakiniku; the owner grills for guests (2022–2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The master cooks and serves the meat, so there are no grills on the tables… Each serving is smaller than average, at about half the size of portions in other restaurants, allowing you to try a variety of dishes." — September 2024.
"Both the yukke and tataki were incredibly fresh and delicious! What's more, the owner grills the meat for you!" — August 2026.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ(店舗会員): 焼肉P貴之助、大阪市中央区宗右衛門町6-25、なんば駅から徒歩5分、毎日18:00〜翌2:00、休みは変わることも、カード・電子マネー・QR不可、カウンター6席、20人まで貸切可、喫煙可。口コミ(2022年12月〜2026年8月): 細い路地の隠れ家、一人でも入りやすい、ユッケとハラミ、焼き加減がちょうどいい、見た目より味の多彩なメニュー、白センマイは数が少ない、朝3時まで、カウンターのみ、マスターが焼いてくれる、韓国風冷奴、センマイ刺しにごま油と塩、味噌、塩タン、ほほ、ミノ、旧清流会館とホテルの隣の路地、ヒロミヤの隣、7人ほどで満席、量は半分ほどで品数を楽しめる、炙りユッケ、和牛たたき、和牛カルビ。

cultural_comfort.note: Six-seat counter; the owner grills.

osaka_ikareta_noodle_fish_tons.hours_raw: Daily 11:00–15:00 (L.O. 14:55) and 18:00–22:00 (L.O. 21:55); Saturday morning ramen 7:00–9:00; open through to the New Year break, check social media (Tabelog). One bowl per person; no eating while looking at phones (Tabelog). Cards, e-money and QR accepted (Tabelog).
osaka_ikareta_noodle_fish_tons.notes: [Ramen · Shinmachi's Ramen 100 seafood-tonkotsu tsukemen] A tsukemen shop near Nishi-Ohashi, open since 2017 and picked for Tabelog's Ramen OSAKA 100 in 2023, 2024 and 2025. The dipping sauce is thick pork bone and seafood, bonito-forward, and it clings to homemade thick, flat noodles chilled in water for a chewy, wheaty bite. Add diced onion and aji daikon as you go, then finish with soup or Dive Rice, a small bowl of rice with green onion to drop into the sauce. The TOKYO-X premium tsukemen (¥1,500) carries juicy rare chashu. There's also a seafood tonkotsu ramen (¥1,000) with a free large size. On Saturdays there is a 7 am morning ramen, such as a charcoal-grilled chashu miso. Noodles were too soft for one pair. Expect a short line at lunch. House rules: one bowl each, no phones while eating.

chef_bio.background: Tsukemen shop (Tabelog, staff-maintained); Tabelog Ramen OSAKA 100 2023, 2024 and 2025.

anecdotes.text: "The broth is a rich seafood and pork bone base, thick and hearty, with a strong flavor of both seafood and pork. The noodles are homemade, flat, and thick." — October 2026, ajitama tsukemen.
"The broth is a double soup made from chicken and pork bones, lightly emulsified with ginger and kombu kelp… The chashu is charcoal-grilled and hung to dry." — October 2026, Saturday morning ramen.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: 食べログ(店舗会員): いかれたヌードル フィッシュトンズ、大阪市西区新町1-25-18 レナジア新町ビル 1F、西大橋駅2番出口から徒歩2分、四ツ橋駅から徒歩3分、毎日11:00〜15:00(L.O.14:55)・18:00〜22:00(L.O.21:55)、土曜は朝ラーメン7:00〜9:00、年末年始まで休まず営業、SNSで確認を、一人一杯、スマホを見ながらの食事は不可、カード・電子マネー・QR可、14席(カウンター10、2人テーブル2)、2017年12月16日開店、食べログ ラーメン OSAKA 百名店2023・2024・2025。口コミ(2026年10月): 雨の週末13時に行列、味玉つけ麺、濃厚な魚介豚骨、自家製の平打ち太麺、玉ねぎとあじ大根、Dive Rice、チャーシュー、炭火焼きチャーシューの味噌ラーメン(朝ラー)、鶏と豚骨のダブルスープ、生姜と昆布、TOKYO-X特製つけ麺1,500円、レアチャーシュー、スープ割り、水で締めた太麺、ラーメンOSAKA 2025、平日21時半は待ちなし、魚介豚骨ラーメン1,000円、鰹節が強い、中太麺か細麺、大盛り無料、麺が柔らかすぎたという声。

osaka_seimenya_nipponbashi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: chicken broth, niboshi, chashu.
osaka_seimenya_nipponbashi.hours_raw: Mon and Wed–Fri 11:00–15:00; Sat–Sun 11:00–16:00; closed Tuesday; hours may change (Tabelog). Ticket machine (August–October 2026). PayPay accepted; no cards or e-money (Tabelog). Families and wheelchair users welcome (Tabelog).
osaka_seimenya_nipponbashi.notes: [Ramen · a two-person tsukemen shop at the south end of Otaroad] A 13-seat noodle shop at the southern tip of Nipponbashi's Otaroad, open since 2013 and run by two: a chef in the kitchen and one person serving, both notably polite. The draw is chicken-shoyu tsukemen (¥1,330 for medium): smooth, glossy noodles and a gentle soy dipping sauce full of chicken, with tenkasu and black shichimi, mild enough to drink on its own. There's also chicken paitan on medium-thick curly noodles; this autumn it carried a curry ball you break into the broth. In summer the chilled niboshi soba (¥1,250) comes with a rice to drown in the cold broth. One bowl took about 15 minutes. Lunch only; closed Tuesdays.

chef_bio.background: Two-person tsukemen and ramen shop on Otaroad (2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The soy sauce-based dipping sauce was not too strong and incredibly delicious!… I personally prefer a gentler flavor that I could drink on its own." — October 2026, chicken-shoyu tsukemen.
"I was advised to pour the broth over the rice, giving it a chilled chazuke-like experience. The furikake sprinkled on the rice added a nice accent." — August 2026, chilled niboshi soba.

osaka_kawachiriba_minamisenba.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: wheat noodles; shoyu tare; clam tsukudani.
osaka_kawachiriba_minamisenba.hours_raw: Lunch only: Mon–Sat and days before/after holidays 11:00–14:30; closed Sundays and holidays (Tabelog). Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog).
osaka_kawachiriba_minamisenba.notes: [Ramen · clam-broth chuka soba for lunch near Nagahoribashi] An eight-seat lunch counter near Nagahoribashi, open since 2021, built on a clear shellfish broth. The kaidashi shio ramen tastes most clearly of clam, light yet deep. The asari shoyu is lighter still, too subtle for some, and the shichimi from Sakai's Yamatsu Tsujita lifts it. Smooth, chewy noodles are the constant praise; one diner ordered extra noodles. Thin chashu, seasoned egg and menma complete the bowl, and the shio set adds rice with clam tsukudani; sansho on the counter suits it. There's also a meat soba, and it once served cold pasta. A calm room. Lunch only, Monday to Saturday. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Clam-broth chuka soba, lunch only (Tabelog, staff-maintained).

anecdotes.text: "The broth was a beautifully clear clam soup, and the noodles were smooth and delicious!… The clam tsukudani (sweet simmered clams) was also great with both the rice and ramen." — September 2026, shio set.
"You can really taste the clam broth in this shio ramen. The richness is sufficient even without changing the flavor of the soup." — June 2026.

osaka_gyukotsu_ou_minamisenba.notes: [Ramen · a one-person beef-bone counter near Nagahoribashi] A nine-seat counter open since 2016, run single-handed by the owner, serving beef-bone ramen until midnight. The broth is rich yet clean, with no off-flavor, and one diner called it richer than tonkotsu. The recommended shio bowl and the white broth come over thin straight noodles that one diner likened to Hong Kong wonton noodles, topped with tender beef tendon or stew-soft chashu, fragrant fried garlic chips, sesame and pickled ginger. Extra noodles are free, or rice at lunch. Summer brought a chilled bowl with pork shabu-shabu, aosa and lemon. Service is warmer than the name suggests: one diner was seen off at the door. Buy a ticket at the machine; PayPay accepted.

chef_bio.background: Beef-bone ramen counter run by the owner alone (May 2026 review).

"The fragrant fried garlic chips are the standout feature of this restaurant, adding an incredible aroma that makes you want to eat more." — May 2026, shio beef-bone ramen.

osaka_aoba_ramen_honmamonya.notes: [Ramen · kakuni and bok choy shoyu ramen by Matsuyamachi] A ten-seat counter 100 m from Matsuyamachi Station, run single-handed by a polite owner, with a spotless room. The Aoba ramen (¥1,700) is the reason to come. A light soy broth of chicken feet and vegetables with Japanese dashi carries medium-thin straight noodles. On top sit two slabs of sweet, meltingly tender kakuni, plus bok choy, a hard-boiled egg and a whole stick of menma. Skip the kakuni for ¥1,100, or go to five slices for ¥2,700. A newer pork-trotter soba with scallion oil (¥1,000) brings three trotters on the side. House condiments let you layer the flavor. It opens at noon, late for ramen. Cards and cashless accepted.

osaka_kitakata_bannai_namba_nipponbashi.notes: [Ramen · Kitakata-style chashu ramen between Nipponbashi and Ebisucho] A branch of the Bannai chain, open since 2023 and one of the few places in Kansai for Kitakata ramen. The bowl is a light, clear pork broth seasoned with soy, over flat, chewy, high-hydration curly noodles. Melt-in-the-mouth chashu and thick-cut green onion top it. The roast pork ramen was ¥1,360 in September 2026. From 1 September the Mega Chashu ramen piles on about 24 slices, nearly double. There's also a miso ramen that won over one shoyu loyalist, a limited chicken shio with yuzu, and a mini aburi yakiniku don. Friendly staff; it was quiet at 22:00 one Friday. Buy a ticket at the machine. Open until 22:00.

osaka_menya_gaten_z_otaroad.notes: [Ramen · Jiro-style mazesoba on Otaroad] A Jiro-style mazesoba counter on Otaroad, open since 2017; one regular also goes to the Namba branch. The MAZE soba comes with 300 g of thick, smooth noodles and tender chashu, and noodles, vegetables, garlic and fat can be adjusted for free. Garlic hits hard, so go light before a meeting. The Taiwanese version (¥1,150) adds ground meat, chives, nori, fish powder and egg yolk; there's a mildly hot curry mazesoba and a brothless shio ramen with yuzu that one fan rates the best of its kind. The counter is stocked with black pepper, shichimi, Sichuan pepper, chili oil and vinegar, kimchi is free, and a ¥100 gacha picks a surprise topping like mentaiko. Allow ten minutes. Cash-only ticket machine.

chef_bio.background: Mazesoba shop on Otaroad (Tabelog, staff-maintained); a Namba branch also operates (May 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The noodles were soft, wide, and flat, topped with ground meat, chives, seaweed, fish powder, garlic, green onions, and an egg yolk, giving it a Jiro-style twist." — February 2026, Taiwanese MAZE soba ¥1,150.
"The 100 yen gacha topping added a playful element, and I was lucky enough to get mentaiko, which paired wonderfully with the rich mazesoba." — May 2026, shoyu mazesoba.

osaka_mugen_ramen_nambanaka3.notes: [Ramen · Mugen's beef-bone shop in Nambanaka 3-chome] A Mugen Ramen shop open since 2020 near Daikokucho, whose beef-bone aroma greets you at the door. The beef-bone white soup ramen is rich and creamy, topped with tender roast beef and fatty brisket. The spicy chashu noodles (¥1,350) add Sichuan pepper, garlic chives and heat a little milder than Shin Ramyun. Opinions split: one diner found it phenomenal, one found the chashu tough and over-seasoned, another didn't think it worth the price, and the mini chashu rice bowl was mushy and salty for one diner. Staff and customers are mostly from overseas, and service was slow for one diner. Open until 23:00. See also Mugen Ramen Sennichimae and Shinsaibashi.

osaka_yakitori_mumei_no_name.notes: [Yakitori · a seven-seat Tajima-chicken counter in Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A dark, grown-up yakitori counter on the fourth floor of a Higashi-Shinsaibashi building, open since 2024 behind an understated sign. Tajima chicken is grilled over charcoal in front of you with refined, light seasoning. The ¥9,000 omakase runs eight skewers, three appetizers and a finish. It opens on seared thigh with fresh pepper, then breast, crunchy gizzard, salt-crisped skin, heart in a sweet tare, tsukune with a rich egg, a boned wing with zucchini, and negima. In between come a liver pâté that won over one liver skeptic, a chicken-broth chawanmushi and homemade pickles. Finish with yakitori don, grilled rice-ball soup or soboro don. À la carte works too. Reserve; closed Wednesdays.

osaka_sakana_shimada.notes: [Japanese · a seasonal fish counter in Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A small, calm Japanese restaurant on a third floor in Higashi-Shinsaibashi, built around seasonal fish. Order à la carte or book an omakase from ¥10,000 ahead. Sashimi might be kensaki squid, tuna, hamo and Wakayama octopus. A January visit brought soy-grilled cod milt, fried oysters and a salmon kasujiru; an August one, abalone, a fragrant dobin mushi and a miso-grilled fish to close. The small dishes are built for sake. The counter is intimate: with no other guests, one diner felt the chef was listening in. Guests are seen to the elevator. Reviewers spent about ¥10,000–30,000.

chef_bio.background: Seasonal fish counter (Tabelog, staff-maintained).

osaka_nihonshuya_ichiro.notes: [Bar · a sake bar behind an unmarked third-floor door] A sake bar on the third floor of the White Building, open since 2015 behind a door that shows nothing of the inside, a little daunting at first. Inside are a counter, a table and a warm welcome. Sake pours by the masu, about a full 180 ml for ¥800–1,000, from labels such as Ishizuchi, Utsukushihime and a limited Kujiranami. The snacks stand out: simmered Saga beef offal that won over a tripe skeptic, tamahimo-ni, simmered sardines, chashu, and tempura of firefly squid or pumpkin. Weekdays bring regulars, weekends overseas visitors, and the TV shows baseball or racing. Weekends and holidays it opens at 2 pm for daytime drinking. Smoking allowed.

chef_bio.background: Sake bar; regulars on weekdays, overseas visitors on weekends, per the owner (December 2025 review).

anecdotes.text: "The simmered offal is absolutely fantastic! It seems to be made with Saga beef offal… Especially the honeycomb tripe, which is one type of offal I usually dislike, but this completely changed my perception." — October 2025.

osaka_steak_house_juju.notes: [Steak · a quiet teppan counter on Dotonbori's west end] A basement teppanyaki counter just west of Midosuji, open since 2009, quieter than its Dotonbori address suggests and used for celebrations. Behind a heavy door, a veteran chef grills at the 11-seat counter and chats as the courses unfold. Expect a salad with two homemade dressings, grilled vegetables and tofu, live kuruma ebi from the tank (head and legs crisped for the wine), sazae, with abalone in the tank too, and a grilled Hokkaido caciocavallo. The main is Kagoshima tenderloin, with paper-thin garlic crisped in butter, homemade garlic soy and ponzu; one diner prefers it to the fattier ribeye. Reviewers spent about ¥8,000–15,000. A 10% service charge applies. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Teppanyaki counter; the chef grills and talks with guests (2023–2025 reviews); official site steak-jyu-jyu.com.

anecdotes.text: "The steak was served with thinly sliced garlic grilled with a generous amount of butter and low heat… It was served with homemade garlic soy sauce, ponzu, and coarsely ground black pepper." — March 2023, Kagoshima chateaubriand.
"The ribeye has a good amount of fat, but I recommend the tenderloin." — April 2025.

osaka_sushi_kiwami_higashishinsaibashi.notes: [Sushi · a sushi kaiseki counter in Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A modern sushi counter at the back of a building's ground floor, open since 2021 behind a noren, with amber light on the counter and private tables with sliding doors. The ¥22,000 omakase runs 15 to 18 items, mixing Edomae sushi with kaiseki dishes. It opens with fig tempura and ginger. Then come kombu-cured flounder and botan shrimp, shima-aji, a fragrant seared scallop roll with sudachi, and Hokkaido uni served in a glass. Kinmedai, nodoguro, toro and marinated akami follow, with seasonal tempura and a sukiyaki-style pot where cotton candy melts in. It closes with a toro-taku roll and a wasanbon pudding. A 10% service charge applies. Hard to find; reserve by phone.

osaka_ramen_seigo_minamisenba.notes: [Ramen · sea-bream shio by Nagahoribashi] A clean, white-wood counter near Nagahoribashi, open since 2021 and serving until midnight. The signature sea-bream shio ramen (¥1,000) is a delicate seafood stock of iriko, kombu and aji, topped with grilled sea bream in place of chashu, over Hokkaido-wheat noodles. To one diner it was refined and deep; to another, too mild, with a strong fish note and little punch. A miso ramen rivals the big miso chains, and a beef-bone shoyu is sweet and light yet deep. Rice bowls and kara-age round out a long ticket-machine menu. Late-night drinkers stop in after a night out. Closed Sundays and holidays; it can sell out.

chef_bio.background: Ramen shop (Tabelog, staff-maintained).

anecdotes.text: "The broth is a delicate seafood stock carefully extracted from selected ingredients such as iriko (dried sardines), kombu kelp, and aji (horse mackerel)… The noodles are made from specially selected Hokkaido wheat." — August 2025, sea-bream shio ramen ¥1,000.
"The idea of using sea bream instead of chashu was interesting and creative, but it wasn't seasoned or salted, and the fish flavor was a bit too strong for my personal taste." — January 2026.

osaka_ninniku_ramen_tenyo_shinmachi.notes: [Ramen · garlic tonkotsu and miso by Nishi-Ohashi] A spacious, clean garlic-ramen shop a minute from Nishi-Ohashi, open since 2021. The base is tonkotsu loaded with chopped garlic over curly noodles, with boldly seasoned chashu good enough to eat with rice; the plain ramen is ¥900. Most reviewers order miso: smooth and mild enough for miso skeptics, also in a garlic miso chashu bowl piled with chashu and a boiled egg, and a spicy miso K ramen (¥1,100). There's also a Kyoto Kujo negi ramen. Garlic can be skipped, reduced, or doubled with an extra side plate. Without it, one diner found the miso merely average. The takana with fresh rice is a quiet star. Closed Sundays.

osaka_hinatsuya_nambanaka.notes: [Ramen · a tonkotsu shop with free rice, next door to Mugen] A tonkotsu ramen shop opened in June 2025, easy to miss beside Mugen Ramen but preferred by at least one diner. The tonkotsu (¥850) is a creamy, slightly frothy white broth, sweet with pork, over thin straight noodles. Seared fatty chashu, a soft-boiled egg, green onion and a sheet of nori top it; one bowl had five quail eggs. Some find it on the light, mild side and a little salty. The value is the draw: rice, one extra noodles, kimchi and onions come free, so wrap rice in soup-soaked nori or add doubanjiang. The vegetable ramen (¥1,000) is heaped with cabbage. Fried rice and a kara-age set too. Cash only; open until 23:00.

"The tonkotsu ramen was JPY 850, and with a free rice and one free extra noodle option, plus unlimited kimchi, the cost performance is excellent." — October 2026.

osaka_kappa_ramen_honpo_namba_parks_sout.notes: [Ramen · Kappa's Namba Parks South branch, with an ULTRA-rich bowl] The Namba Parks South branch of Kappa Ramen Honpo, open since 2023 in a bright, roomy space. The exclusive here is the ULTRA rich: a thick, fatty tonkotsu that clings to medium-thick curly noodles. The regular Kappa ramen comes light or rich, the Aka Kappa adds a gentle chili kick to the tonkotsu shoyu, and the vegetable ramen comes white and sweet or spicy red with chili oil. Every bowl earns a free extra-noodles coupon, thin and firm, with firmness to order. Kimchi, fresh garlic and fried garlic are free. Pair it with a half fried-rice or kara-age set. Order on your phone; lines can form at peak times. Open 10:00 to midnight. See also Kappa Sennichimae and Amemura.

osaka_yuai_tei_nipponbashi.notes: [Ramen · Nipponbashi's Ramen 100 shoyu specialist, daytime only] A shoyu-ramen specialist near Ebisucho, open since 2014 and picked for Tabelog's Ramen OSAKA 100 from 2023 to 2025. Its six bowls are named like a boxer's punches. The classic Right Straight (¥1,050) blends dark and light soy into a rich, mellow, never-salty broth with a depth one regular could drink endlessly, over noodles with a good bite. Add the Unchained Custom (+¥100) of garlic, chive kimchi and habanero for a kick, or pile on menma, butter and a soft-boiled egg. The chashu is thick and tender, though one regular found it too fatty on recent visits. Order rice (¥200) to finish in the soup. Expect a line at lunch. Open 11:00 to 17:30 only; closed Mondays.

osaka_menya_taku_kitahorie.notes: [Ramen · Kitahorie's Ramen 100 wafu tori-ton] A 12-seat counter in Kitahorie, open since 2009 and picked for Tabelog's Ramen OSAKA 100 in 2023, 2024 and 2025 (tenth in 2025, by one account). The signature wafu tori-ton (¥1,000) is a slightly thick blend of chicken and pork bone finished with Japanese dashi on a soy base: rich yet light, with bonito aroma. Thin straight noodles carry a fragrant wheat flavor. On top: thick chashu torched for smokiness, a half egg, green onion, shredded chili and nori heaped with bonito flakes, which scatter if you blow on the noodles. The tori-ton tsukemen comes on thick, wheaty noodles, and there's mazesoba. Buy a ticket outside. It fills fast around noon. Closed Wednesdays.

chef_bio.background: Ramen and tsukemen shop (Tabelog, staff-maintained); Tabelog Ramen OSAKA 100 2023, 2024 and 2025.

anecdotes.text: "The broth seemed to be a blend of chicken and pork bone, finished with a Japanese-style dashi. It was slightly thick and rich yet still light, with a deep flavor that made it hard to stop using my spoon." — September 2026, wafu tori-ton with extra meat ¥1,250.
"The dipping sauce was incredibly rich, packed with the concentrated flavors of chicken and pork… The noodles were thick and had a strong wheat aroma." — October 2026, tori-ton tsukemen.

osaka_furan_ken_honmachi.notes: [Ramen · Tokyo-style chan-kei chuka soba in Honmachi] A rare Osaka take on Tokyo's chan-kei chuka soba, five minutes from Honmachi, open since 2020 in a clean, stylish room; the operator site is the same as Tori Soba Zagin's. The chuka soba (¥800) comes with a generous pour of traditional soy broth over flat noodles, tender chashu, finely cut menma and crisp green onion; soak a ¥150 rice in it. One regular wished the noodles were chewier. The zaru-style cold chuka (¥900) dips straight, slippery noodles into a soy broth, brightened with the niboshi vinegar on the table. Tsukemen, fluffy, strongly seasoned fried rice and a grilled kara-age set fill out the menu. Lunch lines can move slowly. Open daily to 22:30.

osaka_menya_yuu_honmachi.notes: [Ramen · additive-free tori-gyo-ton ramen and tsukemen in Honmachi] An 11-seat counter around an open kitchen near Honmachi, open since 2016 and busy with a line at lunch. Signed celebrity cards cover the walls. The house broth blends chicken, fish and pork without additives into a rich, slightly frothy soup where the fish stays in the background, now topped with bonito flakes. The ramen comes with thick straight noodles, and the chashu version piles on tender pork and green onion. Tsukemen is just as popular: thick curly noodles, regular or a hefty 500 g, with a fragrant niboshi dip. There's also a chicken paitan tsukemen sharpened with black vinegar, plus mazesoba. Add takana rice for ¥90. One diner found it decent but not distinctive. Buy a ticket inside, then wait.

chef_bio.background: Additive-free ramen and tsukemen shop (Tabelog, staff-maintained; 2026 reviews).

osaka_kyosakatei_shinsaibashi.notes: [Japanese · lunch-to-late Japanese courses off Shinsaibashi-suji] A calm second-floor Japanese restaurant just inside Mitsudera-suji, unusual for serving from lunch until 1 am. At lunch the wagyu sukiyaki hitsumabushi gozen (¥3,800) puts A5 kuroge ribeye over rice, eaten plain, then changed up halfway, then finished with dashi poured from a flask. Evenings are courses only, around ¥10,000 and generous. A winter course brought Matsuba crab with its roe, ankimo in a crisp monaka shell, fragrant katsuo tataki and unagi-maki; the chef will also pace seafood, meat, hot pot and rice to your appetite and take requests. Finish with shaved ice in homemade syrup. Friendly staff, and international guests too. Closed Sundays.

osaka_nihonshu_awa_hozenji.notes: [Bar · a sake bar upstairs from Tempura Tenzan in Hōzenji Yokocho] A hidden sake bar on the second floor above Tempura Tenzan, opened in July 2025, with a calm, modern Japanese room and sake served in kiriko cut glass. Start with the tasting set of three (¥1,980), which has paired Hakkaisan, Tenzan and Gohshun, then move on to premium bottles like Juyondai and Dassai. Whisky, wine and fruit cocktails are on hand too, and food can be ordered from the tempura restaurant downstairs, which makes it an easy second stop after dinner below. The master is chatty and attentive. It's popular with overseas visitors, and one sake fan found the prices set for tourists. Open until 3 am; closed Wednesdays.

osaka_wine_dining_quatre.notes: [Italian · a sommelier's basement wine dining bar in Souemoncho] A cozy basement wine bar in Souemoncho, open since 2017, with a few counter seats and one table and a sommelier who picks bottles to taste and budget; one group asked for something reasonable and got an exceptional bottle. Start with the generous appetizer platter of about eight small dishes, bruschetta and a cold soup among them, then go to the pastas: uni (one diner's dish of the night), mentaiko cream, or loaded with karasumi. Risotto, roast duck, roast beef, isaki carpaccio, a seafood pizza and lamb follow, and the vegetables earn praise. Finish with a chocolate parfait. Courses can be set to your budget by phone. Closed Wednesdays.

osaka_sushi_ikkei_higashishinsaibashi.notes: [Sushi · a red-lit late-night sushi counter in Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A casual sushi counter opened in December 2025 among the flashy signs of Higashi-Shinsaibashi, serving until 3 am. Inside, a red-themed counter keeps it relaxed rather than stiff. Order omakase nigiri or graze: eel that one diner loved, jumbo shrimp, a special tuna salad, wagyu tataki, sake-steamed clams, a salmon tasting plate, and a fluffy dashimaki full of dashi. The crab and ikura gunkan come piled to overflowing, though one diner found the taste average next to the looks. Local sake is well stocked. The head chef and staff are friendly, and it has worked for both dates and business meals. No table charge. Closed Wednesdays.

osaka_ushi_zanmai_dotonbori.notes: [Yakiniku · a smoky alley yakiniku off Sennichimae] A small yakiniku restaurant down a narrow alley off the Sennichimae shopping street, open since 2020, whose red lanterns make it look like an izakaya. Meat is grilled on shichirin at the counter or a back table. The outside skirt is the star: one diner rated it above a famous chain's, and another ordered seconds. Also order the garlic-salt tongue, salted tongue, an assorted platter of kuroge wagyu cuts, and kimchi, then finish with piping-hot egg soup (¥440) or bibimbap noodles (¥980). Staff explain the cuts. The aisle is narrow and the room smoky, which is part of the charm. Open until 3 am on Wednesdays and Thursdays; closed Mondays. The newest review is from September 2025.

osaka_matsuya_shokudo_nipponbashi.notes: [Japanese · an old-school shokudo famous for omurice] A nostalgic neighborhood shokudo down a narrow Nipponbashi alley, with metal chairs, a small counter and a second floor, busy even near closing. The most popular dish is the omurice (¥900): chicken rice wrapped in a flawless thin yellow egg with a bold dollop of red ketchup, served with Chinese soup, and there's a large size. The ramen is a classic chuka soba with house-made straight noodles and thick chashu, and the spicy miso ramen comes dark and robust under stir-fried pork and bean sprouts. Fried rice is generous, so consider the half. Prices are low. A short wait at noon; dishes can take 10 to 15 minutes. Lunch to mid-afternoon only, until sold out. Cash only; closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Neighborhood shokudo (2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The vibrant yellow egg enveloped the chicken rice thinly, without any flaws. At its center lay a generous dollop of bright red ketchup, unapologetically bold." — October 2026, omurice.

osaka_seiran_nakadera.notes: [Chinese · a Tabelog 100 Chinese restaurant near Tanimachi 6-chome] A compact Chinese restaurant on a quiet slope near Tanimachi 6-chome, open since 2012 and picked for Tabelog's Chinese WEST 100 in 2021, 2023, 2024 and 2026, more refined than a neighborhood Chinese place. Lunch is the bargain: sets from ¥1,800, or the Seiran lunch (¥2,300) with three appetizers, soup, two original dim sum, a main of sweet-and-sour pork or seafood chili, refillable rice and dessert. The sweet-and-sour pork is the dish people praise most. Dinner is a course around ¥10,000 or à la carte: mapo tofu balancing heat and numbness, soft-shell crab in chili sauce, black-vinegar sweet-and-sour pork. One diner found the dan dan noodles bitter. Lunch fills by sign-up board before opening; book dinner. About seven days off a month.

osaka_men_style_tanimotoke_honmachi.notes: [Ramen · bubbly chicken paitan and shellfish shio by Honmachi] A stylish two-floor ramen shop a minute from Honmachi, open since December 2023, with several styles. The original bubble-style chicken paitan (¥1,380) is a frothy, creamy broth seasoned with soy and a hint of shellfish, lighter than it looks: delicious, but one regular preferred the chicken-and-shellfish shio, slightly sweet with a strong shellfish flavor, which is also served chilled with grilled scallop and a red egg. There's a clam shio with yuzu and a Sapporo-style miso with charbroiled pork, ginger and green onion. Noodles are medium-thick, round and whole-wheat, chewy. There are no condiments on the table. One diner found the yukke rice bowl tiny and the service formal. Buy a ticket out front and wait to be called.

osaka_ramen_daisenso_senba_shinsaibashi.notes: [Ramen · light scallop shoyu with free chashu by the slice in Senba] A spacious, stylish branch of THE RAMEN WAR in Senba Shinsaibashi, open since 2021 and usually busy. The basic Pistol is a light soy broth of chicken and shellfish with a pronounced scallop flavor, clinging to the noodles. The draws are the free extras: choose one to five slices of tender rare chashu (on one visit everyone took five), and a half-serving of extra noodles is free; order it early, as it takes time to cook. Limited bowls rotate, such as the Impulse with chopped onion and plenty of garlic, or the Scallop Launcher, spicy for ¥10 more. Add a chashu rice bowl. About half the customers were from overseas on one visit. Cash only; open until 23:00.

chef_bio.background: Branch of THE RAMEN WAR; official site ramen-daisenso.com (Tabelog, staff-maintained).

anecdotes.text: "I couldn't tell if it was niboshi (dried sardines) or scallops, but the seafood flavor was concentrated in the light soy sauce… I loved that I could choose the number of chashu slices and even add a half serving of noodles." — September 2026, Pistol.

osaka_yamanaka_seimensho_honmachi.notes: [Ramen · house-made noodles and ¥400 fried rice in Honmachi] A counter ramen shop near Sakaisuji-Hommachi, open since 2011 and busy with office workers, with seats turning over fast. The noodles are made in-house and you can choose the firmness; one repeat visitor recommends extra firm. The tonkotsu ramen (¥890) is a rich broth with thin noodles; the shoyu ramen is lighter, with a hint of yuzu and plenty of chopped onion, and one diner liked the tonkotsu shoyu best. The spicy miso ramen (¥1,100) mixes spicy miso into the tonkotsu, and a spicy ramen limited to 10 a day sells out quickly, so arrive before noon. The fried rice (¥400) is generous and praised in several reviews. Pickled ginger is free on the table. Buy a ticket at the door. Cash only; closed Sundays.

osaka_ramen_r_namba.hours_raw: Sat, Sun and Mon open 24 hours; Tue 00:00–04:00 and 11:00–04:00 next day; Wed–Thu 11:00–04:00 next day; Fri 11:00–24:00; no regular holidays (Tabelog, staff-maintained). Ticket machine just inside; water and chopsticks are self-service (official site). Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog).
osaka_ramen_r_namba.notes: [Ramen · a big Jiro-style shop open all night near Ebisucho] A large, clean Jiro-inspired ramen shop between Ebisucho and Namba, open since 2022, with 27 seats including tables. Noodles and broth are made in-house: flat, wavy noodles of Maturité flour that one diner found dense and packed with wheat. A bowl (¥1,200 in October 2026) comes with 100 g to 300 g of noodles for the same price; call your vegetables and fat, and add garlic yourself. Expect a fatty, heavy broth and thick chashu; one diner found the soup too sour, another the pork underheated. There is also R's set meal (¥1,000), which one diner had on a weekend morning: bean sprouts, thick chashu and a fried egg with rice, tonkotsu soup and kimchi. Open 24 hours Saturday to Monday and until 04:00 most other nights. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Jiro-inspired ramen shop with a second shop in Nagai (official site ramen-r.com; Tabelog, staff-maintained).

anecdotes.text: "The flat, wavy noodles made with Maturité have a unique resistance when slurped. They have a dense, hard texture that feels packed with wheat, making them delicious." — October 2026, pork ramen 200 g.
"The dish featured a generous serving of bean sprouts topped with thick slices of chashu and a runny yolk fried egg. It came with white rice, soup, and kimchi." — October 2026, R's set meal ¥1,000.

Ticket machine at the entrance or QR ordering at the table (October 2026). Cards, e-money and PayPay accepted (Tabelog).
osaka_kanfu_ramen_kitakyuhojimachi.notes: [Chinese · Sichuan cooking and knife-cut noodles in the Shinsaibashi arcade] A large Sichuan restaurant in the covered shopping arcade near Honmachi, with many Chinese customers. Lunch is a bargain: a daily set for about ¥780, such as a generous chinjao rosu (pork with green peppers) or mapo eggplant, with soup and dessert, served fast; one repeat visitor returns for the liver and garlic-chive stir-fry. Noodles include knife-cut noodles you can customize with cilantro and garlic, Sichuan dan dan noodles and mapo noodles; add fried rice for ¥400. At night groups can book the all-you-can-eat-and-drink courses (¥3,980 for about 50 dishes in September 2026), with gyoza and oyster with stir-fried lettuce among the hits and seasonings that taste less Japanized. Private rooms with a big round table seat up to 20. Order by ticket or QR code. Cards accepted.

chef_bio.background: Sichuan Chinese restaurant (official site kangfu-osaka.com; Tabelog, staff-maintained).

anecdotes.text: "I was pleased that I could customize my knife-cut noodles with options like cilantro and garlic. The fried rice, which can be added for an extra JPY 400, was surprisingly delicious." — August 2026.
"For JPY 3,980, we enjoyed an all-you-can-eat and drink experience. The cost performance is amazing! We had access to a menu of 50 different dishes." — September 2026.

osaka_men_to_mugen_no_kanosei_honmachi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: back fat, chashu, chicken and scallop broth.
osaka_men_to_mugen_no_kanosei_honmachi.hours_raw: Mon–Fri 11:00–15:00 and 18:00–22:00; Sat 11:00–23:00; Sun 11:00–22:00; breakfast ramen 8:00–11:00 by reservation only (Tabelog or Instagram); breaks possible, continuous-service days posted on Instagram and Google (Tabelog, staff-maintained). Cards, e-money and QR accepted (Tabelog).
osaka_men_to_mugen_no_kanosei_honmachi.notes: [Ramen · Jiro-style mazesoba and a light scallop paitan by Honmachi] A tiny seven-seat counter near Honmachi, open since March 2025 and named as the brand's head shop. The mazesoba (¥1,050) is the draw: thick, chewy, wheaty noodles in a rich sauce with crunchy bean sprouts, onion and crispy garlic chips. Add chopped garlic from the counter, as it can taste flat without, and vinegar near the end; the spicy version (¥1,150, large 300 g) adds plenty of back fat, rare chashu and fried onion. In summer there is a chilled soupless Jiro-style ramen. The chicken paitan (¥950) is the opposite: light and smooth, with scallop broth, chunks of scallop, curly egg noodles and big menma; one diner found it only average. Extra rice is ¥50. Some nights there is a 10-minute wait.

chef_bio.background: Head shop of Men to Mugen no Kanosei, per its name (Tabelog, staff-maintained).

anecdotes.text: "This hearty mazesoba features thick noodles, a rich sauce, and plenty of back fat for a satisfying boost of energy." — October 2026, spicy mazesoba large (300 g).
"When I think of chicken paitan, I usually imagine a rich and creamy flavor, but this soup was surprisingly light." — October 2026.

osaka_sakanaya_kojun_shinsaibashi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: fish-led menu; dashi throughout.
osaka_sakanaya_kojun_shinsaibashi.hours_raw: Weekdays 17:30–24:00 (L.O. 23:00); Sun and holidays 17:30–23:00 (L.O. 22:00); closed Tuesdays (official site). Online reservations for counter seats; phone for tables of three or more (Tabelog, staff-maintained). Service charge added (Tabelog). Cards and PayPay accepted.
osaka_sakanaya_kojun_shinsaibashi.notes: [Japanese · a fish-led izakaya and sake bar run by two off Shinsaibashi-suji] A hidden counter izakaya at the back of a building's ground-floor arcade, open since 2019 and run by two. The owner is a cook of Japanese cuisine and a sommelier, so it suits both sake and wine drinkers: sake from around Japan rotates, and wine is chosen to match what you eat. Fish comes first, with sashimi from the morning's buying, but the menu wanders: the signature, per the shop and one weekly regular, is the keema curry dashimaki (house keema rolled into egg), alongside chicken tempura with tartar, potato salad, salted sweet-potato tempura and sansho rice balls with red miso soup to finish. Seasonal set courses are available by advance booking; one December 2025 course included abalone chawanmushi and an assorted sashimi platter. One regular praises the pacing and attentive but unintrusive service. Book counter seats online; closed Tuesdays.

chef_bio.background: Izakaya run by two; owner a cook of Japanese cuisine and a sommelier (official site kojun.jp).
chef_bio.philosophy: Seasoning made in-house; ingredients bought each morning; counter-first service so the pace suits each guest (official site).

anecdotes.text: "When I first heard about the combination of keema curry and dashimaki, I thought, 'Will that really work together?' But it does. It works incredibly well." — August 2026.

"The fish tartare mentioned in the Tabelog comments was made with Yokowa and tasted as good as pork cutlet… the fried ginkgo nuts were perfectly seasoned with salt. To finish off, we had the sansho rice balls and red miso soup." — October 2026.

osaka_ranpuya_shinsaibashi.gf_detail: Not gluten-free: battered, deep-fried kushikatsu; sauce and lemon soy.
osaka_ranpuya_shinsaibashi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: meat and seafood skewers.
osaka_ranpuya_shinsaibashi.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 16:00–23:00; closed Sundays (Tabelog, staff-maintained). Reservations advised (April 2026). Smoking allowed. Cards, PayPay and Rakuten Pay accepted (Tabelog).
osaka_ranpuya_shinsaibashi.notes: [Japanese · a one-person basement kushikatsu counter on Shinsaibashi-suji] An eight-seat counter down a flight of stairs off the Shinsaibashi-suji arcade, run single-handedly; one diner felt most customers were regulars. Kushikatsu are fried to order and handed over one at a time, so each is crisp; the batter is thin enough that the ingredient shows through, and one diner found not a single miss. Beyond the usual sauce you can dip in shrimp salt or lemon soy. One diner recommends the kelp with roe and the shrimp bread (ebi pan), and another ended with a shrimp-salt rice ball. Portions are small, so you can try many. It's homey: take drinks from the fridge yourself and write down your order. With one person cooking it can feel busy. Book ahead; it fills up. Smoking allowed.

chef_bio.background: Kushikatsu counter run by one person (2024–2026 reviews; Tabelog, staff-maintained).

anecdotes.text: "The kushikatsu is fried right after you order, and each skewer is served one by one, ensuring they are all crispy. The batter is perfectly thin, allowing the flavors of the ingredients to shine through without feeling heavy." — August 2025.

"You can grab drinks from the refrigerator yourself, and you place your orders by writing them down, giving it a very homey feeling… I highly recommend the kombu kelp with roe and the shrimp bread." — November 2024.

osaka_bar_kawana_hozenji.vegan_detail: No vegan information; a bar, not a meal stop.
osaka_bar_kawana_hozenji.hours_raw: Mon–Sat 18:00–01:00; closed Sundays; hours may change (Tabelog). Non-smoking (Tabelog). Seat charge about ¥1,000 (September 2024). Cards (JCB, AMEX, Diners) and QR accepted (Tabelog).
osaka_bar_kawana_hozenji.notes: [Bar · a hidden wood-rich bar up a staircase by Hozenji] A classic bar you would walk past: in a narrow alley near Hozenji, a barely-marked steep staircase leads to a second door and then a warm, wood-rich room with records playing, a counter and a table in back. One reviewer notes that charred marks from a 2002 fire still show on the counter. The drinks list is short but well made: fresh-fruit cocktails squeezed to order, gin and tonic, a short cocktail left to the bartender, whisky such as Bowmore. Snacks are nuts and dried fruit; one diner loved the dried orange slices. Diners describe the master as easygoing and easy to talk to, and it's calm despite Hozenji Yokocho next door, with overseas visitors among the customers. A seat charge applied (about ¥1,000 in 2024); six drinks for two came to ¥7,500 in February 2026. Non-smoking. Mind the stairs.

chef_bio.background: Bar near Hozenji (2024–2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "Inside, where records play, you feel completely separated from the outside world, losing track of both time and daylight." — September 2024.

"I ordered two Bowmore whiskies and a cocktail, and the atmosphere was so pleasant that we just relaxed. The dried orange slices were surprisingly delicious. We had six drinks between the two of us, and the total was JPY 7500." — February 2026.

osaka_sosaku_teppan_gin_sennichimae.vegan_detail: Not vegan: steak, horumon, shrimp and bacon on a shared griddle.

osaka_sosaku_teppan_gin_sennichimae.notes: [Teppanyaki · a casual creative griddle bar in Sennichimae] A small second-floor teppanyaki bar in Sennichimae with a counter and a few tables, casual enough to drop in for a drink. The griddle menu runs to sirloin steak shabu-shabu dipped in ponzu or a sweet yolk sauce, large shrimp grilled until the heads are crisp, horumon, and grilled vegetables that two diners singled out (the onions are sweet). Start with the potato salad topped with thick-cut bacon. Finish with soba-meshi, garlic rice or fried rice, or the honey toast for dessert. One diner found the staff friendly and accommodating. There's wine. Smoking allowed; closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Teppanyaki bar (Tabelog, staff-maintained; 2024–2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "For the sirloin steak shabu-shabu, I was torn between ponzu sauce and a yolk-style sauce. I chose the latter, which was sweet and blended well with the meat… The large shrimp were grilled with the heads crispy." — October 2024.
"The meat was absolutely delicious!! While there is counter seating, it's a very casual place! The fried rice was tasty, and the honey on the toasted bread was exquisite!" — September 2026.

osaka_sea_station_dotonbori.vegan_detail: Not vegan: seafood and meat throughout.
osaka_sea_station_dotonbori.hours_raw: Daily 17:30–24:00 (food L.O. 23:00, drinks 23:30); irregular holidays (Tabelog, staff-maintained; official site). Appetizer charge ¥550 (Tabelog). Cash only: no cards, e-money or QR (Tabelog). Smoking allowed (August 2026).
osaka_sea_station_dotonbori.notes: [Japanese · a fresh-fish izakaya bar over the Dotonbori canal] A fourth-floor izakaya bar right by Dotonbori Bridge, open since 2011, whose windows look out on the canal; the four-seat sofa by the window is the spot. True to the name, fish leads, bought at the market daily: excellent sashimi, crisp katsuo tatsuta-age, marinated mackerel, and a shrimp mapo tofu more than one diner insists you try. The menu runs to 60-plus dishes with Okinawan touches, and an eel rice ball makes a filling finish. Drinks are the other draw, with 200-plus choices, including over 100 sakes a year, which the manager will suggest, plus a good shochu list. The master is friendly. Courses with all-you-can-drink suit groups, up to 30 for private hire. A ¥550 appetizer charge applies; one diner found the billing unclear. Cash only; smoking allowed.

chef_bio.background: Izakaya and dining bar (official site sea-station.net; Tabelog, staff-maintained).
chef_bio.philosophy: Fish bought at the market daily; 200+ drinks (official site).

anecdotes.text: "True to its name, SeaStation offers a plethora of fresh seafood. The sashimi is excellent, and the fried bonito (Katsuo no Tatsuta-age) is crispy and delicious. The eel rice ball served as a finale is quite filling." — August 2026.
"I can't express how much I loved the marinated mackerel… And you absolutely must try the shrimp Mapo Tofu." — September 2023.

osaka_chuka_soba_kazura_awaza.hours_raw: 11:00 (doors around 10:45)–16:00; closed Fridays; New Year closures announced on the listing; hours may change (Tabelog). Cards and QR accepted; no e-money (Tabelog). Three waiting chairs outside (October 2026).
osaka_chuka_soba_kazura_awaza.notes: [Ramen · a Tabelog 100 frothy chicken dashi soba for under ¥700] A nine-seat counter a minute from Honmachi exit 23, open since 2015 and picked for Tabelog's Ramen OSAKA 100 in 2023, 2024 and 2025, famous for big quality at a small price. The dashi soba (¥690 in October 2026) is a foamy, espuma-style chicken paitan with katsuobushi; one diner found bonito flakes settled at the bottom and stirred them in. It's creamy yet not heavy, seasoned with Aichi soy sauces. House-made medium straight noodles are smooth and chewy, and the chashu and egg have a smoky edge. Premium toppings add extra chashu and a seasoned egg for ¥150; a cold soba with roast-pork rice bowl comes in under ¥1,000. Diners report lines of five to eight and 10- to 15-minute waits at lunch, with chairs outside; bowls arrive in about five minutes, and rice can sell out. Lunch only; closed Fridays.

chef_bio.background: Ramen counter; Tabelog Ramen OSAKA 100 2023, 2024 and 2025.

anecdotes.text: "The broth is made from chicken and katsuobushi (dried bonito), creating a slightly thick soy sauce soup… resulting in a creamy, bubbly texture with a rich and refined taste! The noodles are homemade, with a medium thickness and straight shape." — October 2026, dashi soba ¥690.

"As I continued eating, I discovered what seemed to be katsuobushi (dried bonito flakes) settled at the bottom of the bowl. By mixing it in well, the umami of the seafood added depth to the flavor." — October 2026, dashi soba with premium toppings.

osaka_ramen_stand_men_box_honmachi.notes: [Ramen · chicken-and-pork shoyu with house noodles by Sakaisuji-Honmachi] A lively little ramen stand a minute from Sakaisuji-Hommachi, open since 2019, busy with local workers, with hip-hop on the speakers and energetic, attentive staff. The chicken-and-pork shoyu (¥1,000) is the standard: house-made straight noodles, chewy and smooth, in a well-balanced soy broth, with thin chashu, menma, chopped white leek and mitsuba. Shio fans can have the chicken-and-pork shio (large ¥1,100), and there are chicken-only shio and shoyu bowls and a mazesoba. At lunch rice is ¥100 in any size; pair it with the table's "Devil's Garlic", or pickled garlic and mayonnaise, and there are spicy garlic chives too. One diner found it a bit salty. Cash only; closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Ramen stand (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The noodles have a wonderful texture, being both chewy and smooth, with great flavor. The rich umami of the chicken and pork combines perfectly with the expertly balanced soy sauce flavor in the broth." — October 2026, chicken-and-pork shoyu ¥1,000.

"The homemade straight noodles pair perfectly with the broth… With two slices of chashu, menma, plenty of chopped white onions, and mitsuba, the combination is delightful… The pickled garlic and mayonnaise are truly devilish." — October 2026.

osaka_ramen_so_rekishi_o_kizame_nipponba.notes: [Ramen · Osaka's famous Jiro-style line by Ebisucho] The Nipponbashi branch of a well-known Jiro-style name, open since January 2024, with long lines: 15 to 50 people, rain or shine, and 40 minutes to over an hour from joining to eating. Buy your ticket in line. Bowls are thick noodles (150 g to 400 g) under a mountain of crunchy bean sprouts in a rich soy-based pork broth sweet with back fat, piping hot to the end; call your garlic, vegetables and fat, or go "everything extra". There's also a dry ramen, plus toppings like double pork, cheese and egg. The staff are the other draw: energetic, patient with first-timers and cheering you on, but there's a strict no-leftovers policy, so order honestly. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Branch of the Ramen So Rekishi o Kizame Jiro-style shops (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The thick noodles, a mountain of bean sprouts, a rich soy-based pork broth, and the concentrated sweetness and umami of the back fat. Each component is intensely unique, yet they all come together beautifully." — October 2026, 300 g with everything extra.
"The broth was piping hot, and the noodles had the perfect firmness… And look at the perfect boiling of the bean sprouts!" — October 2026, 400 g with double pork, cheese and egg.

osaka_tsukemen_suzume_yuhigaoka.notes: [Ramen · spicy shrimp-miso tsukemen in a chic room near Shitennoji] The Yuhigaoka branch of Suzume, whose main shop is in Amerikamura, open since 2013 a few minutes from Shitennoji-mae Yuhigaoka. The room is dark and stylish, with counter, tables and sofas, roomy for a tsukemen shop. The signature spicy tsukemen (¥1,000, level 1 to 3) has a thick red dip of pork bone and dried mackerel blended with miso, chilies, chili oil and shrimp, nicely balanced between seafood and heat, and it stays warm. Noodles are medium-thick and chewy, 200 g or 300 g, with thick pork-belly chashu and a seasoned egg; finish with the yuzu soup. The ajitama tsukemen is the classic, and one diner had the hot-noodle version for ¥950. Grilled gyoza on the side. Buy a ticket at the door. Cash only; open daily.

chef_bio.background: Branch of Tsukemen Suzume (main shop in Amerikamura).

anecdotes.text: "The rich dipping sauce features a base extracted from carefully selected pork bones and dried mackerel, blended with miso, several types of chili peppers, chili oil, and shrimp, resulting in a thick, red sauce." — September 2026, spicy tsukemen.
"The tsukemen here never gets boring, and I love that the dipping sauce stays warm for a long time!" — October 2026, spicy tsukemen ¥1,000, level 2, 300 g.

osaka_menya_zuzuzuito_bakuromachi.notes: [Ramen · clear iriko shio and charcoal chashu by Matsuyamachi] A small, wood-toned shop by the Yokobori River, open since March 2026 and already featured in Ramen Walker, with a posted note about its additive-free cooking. The shio ramen (¥950) is the lead: a clear dashi of Ibuki iriko, mackerel flakes, kombu and dried shiitake, finished with salt tare and a shellfish oil, light but full of seafood umami. House-made thin straight noodles of Hokkaido wheat are chewy; chashu is grilled over charcoal on a shichirin. The special shio (¥1,380) brings four chashu cuts, and the wontons (shio wonton ¥1,280) are plump and juicy; one diner ranks them among the best in Osaka. The shoyu blends two soy sauces; one diner found it less striking than the shio. Weekday waits were short; Sunday afternoon was packed.

chef_bio.background: Ramen shop (Tabelog, staff-maintained); featured in Ramen Walker (October 2026 review).
chef_bio.philosophy: No additives, per the shop's posted note (October 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The broth was a delightful seafood soup made from Ibuki iriko, upper mackerel flakes, genuine kombu, and domestic dried shiitake mushrooms, combined with a special salt sauce. The soup was light yet packed with the umami of seafood, enhanced by fried green onions and yuzu." — October 2026, shio wonton ¥1,280.

"The chashu, grilled over charcoal in a shichirin (Japanese grill), is exceptional, offering a live cooking experience along with a delightful smokiness and concentrated flavor." — October 2026, special shio ¥1,380.

osaka_torigara_shoyu_juujisei_minamihonm.notes: [Ramen · a light chicken shoyu with tuna bonito, open past midnight in Honmachi] A small counter shop near Honmachi, open since 2023, that serves lunch and then reopens at 19:00 until after midnight, handy after drinks. The default bowl is the white-shoyu maguro-bushi ramen (¥1,030): a light soy broth of chicken bones and niboshi lifted with tuna-bonito flakes, with medium-thin straight noodles, chashu and a generous heap of crunchy wood-ear mushroom, green onion and bean sprouts; add katsuobushi halfway to change the flavor. The yuzu ramen is lighter still. In summer there was a chilled salt-shoyu with lemon-pickled onion and prosciutto (¥800). Portions are modest, so pair it with the kara-age and half fried rice set (¥600). Buy a ticket at the machine. Closed Saturdays.

chef_bio.background: Ramen counter (Tabelog; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The broth was a light soy flavor made from chicken bones and niboshi (dried sardines), combined with bonito flakes, resulting in a refreshing taste that was perfect for a late-night meal after drinks. "The bowl was refreshingly chilled, featuring straight thin noodles, onion pickles, prosciutto, and black pepper." — August 2026, chilled salt-shoyu ramen ¥800.

osaka_shisen_tantanmen_daruma_senba.notes: [Ramen · Sichuan tantanmen and ¥50 fried rice under the Senba Center Building] A tantanmen specialist two floors down in the Senba Center Building, open since 2024 and packed at weekday lunch, quieter on Saturdays. Four kinds of tantanmen with adjustable heat: the new white sesame (¥950) is rich in sesame with a strong Sichuan-spice note, labelled mild but hot enough for one diner; there's also a dry tantanmen that comes with rice. A regular swears by the hot-and-sour noodles, tangy and numbing more than fiery. The deal that people write about is the ¥50 add-on with any noodle: half fried rice or a mapo rice bowl. Pan-fried gyoza are good too, and staff are friendly. Follow the Instagram for a free seasoned egg. Closed Sundays.

anecdotes.text: "The hot and sour noodles are delicious every time I have them; they're not overly spicy, but the tanginess and numbing sensation are irresistible." — July 2026, fourth visit.

osaka_menya_yamahide_sakaisuji_honmachi.notes: [Ramen · Taiwan mazesoba with oi-meshi, open late by Sakaisuji-Honmachi] A small counter a minute from Sakaisuji-Hommachi exit 6, open since 2016 and part of a brand that also has a Nara shop. The draw is the Taiwan mazesoba (¥900, regular or small, garlic to taste): spicy Taiwan-style minced pork with green onion, garlic chives, garlic and chili, balanced by egg, on thick chewy noodles that hold the toppings. Mix hard, change it up with kombu vinegar, then follow the house routine for oi-meshi: leave the spoon in your empty bowl, set it on the counter, and ask for rice (¥50) to mop up the rest. There's also a spicy ramen with grilled chashu that one diner found lighter than it looks. The master is friendly. Open until 02:00 on weeknights; cash only.

osaka_enge_spice_sennichimae.notes: [Chinese · a spice izakaya with craft gin, open until 05:00 on weekends] An alley izakaya in Sennichimae, open since 2020, that layers aroma rather than raw heat onto familiar Chinese dishes. The house favorites are the yodare-dori, tender chicken in a nutty sesame-spice sauce, and the iron-pot mapo tofu; diners also praise the shrimp chili, the spicy lamb stir-fry and even the kimchi, and small plates let you try many. Spice curries close the night, rotating flavors such as chicken neck with tomato, Akashi octopus, or duck keema with shiso and umeboshi; on some days there's a curry lunch, which one eight-time regular calls the best in Osaka. More than 20 craft gins are matched to the food, and staff are generous with recommendations. Hot-pot courses come with two hours of drinks. Seating is a bit tight. Open until 24:00, Fridays and Saturdays until 05:00.

chef_bio.background: Spice izakaya, "Chinese × spice" concept (official site engespice.com; Tabelog, staff-maintained).
chef_bio.philosophy: Aroma over heat, so the flavors carry through the meal and suit drinks (official site).
chef_bio.specialty: Yodare-dori; iron-pot mapo tofu; spice curry; craft gin.

anecdotes.text: "The tender chicken was complemented by a rich sauce with a nutty sesame flavor and a hint of spices… Personally, I was impressed by the spicy lamb stir-fry." — September 2026.

osaka_tonkatsu_imanara_sennichimae.notes: [Japanese · low-temperature tonkatsu of Watanabe Berkshire pork in Sennichimae] A small counter-and-table tonkatsu shop in Sennichimae, open since 2024, built around Watanabe Berkshire pork from Kagoshima, with the lighter Imoko SPF pork as the alternative (a menu chart and the shop's own manga explain the difference). Cutlets are fried low then high, so allow about 20 minutes; the reward is tender, juicy meat, and one diner called the tenderloin the most tender tonkatsu ever. The Spencer roll (ribeye) is the rich choice. Taste it with rock salt, dashi soy, mustard or the house sauce, which has a slight curry note; one diner preferred salt. Cabbage with a carrot-and-perilla dressing can be refilled, and the pork miso soup is good. Many customers are from overseas; ordering is by QR code. Tables are cramped. Open daily.

chef_bio.background: Tonkatsu shop (Tabelog, staff-maintained); sister shop Tonkatsu Shiga in Namba Sennichimae (listing).

anecdotes.text: "The menu chart was easy to understand, showcasing the rich Watanabe Berkshire alongside the lighter Imoko pork… Since it's cooked at a low temperature, I waited about 20 minutes." — August 2026, Watanabe Berkshire Spencer roll set 180 g.

osaka_jizakana_tempura_urokoya_higashish.notes: [Japanese · rare local fish, sashimi and tempura off Mitsudera-suji] A hidden fish izakaya at the back of a building on Mitsudera-suji, open since 2018: noisy street outside, calm room inside, with a handwritten menu. The draw is fish you rarely see, much of it from Owase in Mie; the sashimi platter is full of names one diner had never heard, all very fresh. Tempura is crisp and often unusual, and grilled fish comes crunchy outside and fluffy inside. Add oysters with ponzu, then finish with a grilled rice ball, a tempura rice bowl or Inaniwa udon. A wide sake list is fairly priced. A ¥5,500 course was offered in late 2024. Diners praise the well-timed service, and one regular says every friend introduced keeps coming back. Smoking allowed; closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Fish and tempura izakaya (Tabelog, staff-maintained).

osaka_ohara_hiroshimayaki_nishishinsaiba.notes: [Okonomiyaki · a one-person Hiroshima-style griddle on the edge of Amerikamura] A small, long-running okonomiyaki spot on the quiet side of Amerikamura, where the owner cooks, serves and takes payment alone. The specialty is Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki, layered and packed with cabbage; one regular calls it the best in Osaka, and the soba niku tama double comes with crispy fried noodles and a spicy sauce. Around it is a cheap, beer-friendly teppan menu: teppan kimchi with beef intestine, beef sinew with ponzu, fried squid legs, octopus and scallops, shio yakisoba. In summer the draft beer comes in a frozen mug. The owner can seem reserved at first; one diner found it cool, another found real warmth by the end. Prices are low; cash only; open until 01:00, closed Sundays.

osaka_sumibiyaki_nedoko_shinsaibashi.notes: [Japanese · unsteamed Kansai-style charcoal eel and eel skewers by Shinsaibashi] An eel specialist on Mitsudera-suji, open since 2007 and featured on TV (Matsuko no Shiranai Sekai, 2022). Eel, mainly the Kiso Sansen brand, is killed to order and grilled over charcoal in the Kansai jiyaki style without steaming, so the skin is crisp and the flesh fluffy, with a tare that isn't too sweet and Wakayama sansho. The unaju comes on a round lidless plate so steam doesn't soften the skin. What sets it apart is the eel skewers, rare in Osaka: belly, neck, burdock roll and more, from ¥880 each or five for ¥4,180; smoked eel goes well with sake. Monthly omakase courses (¥8,800 and ¥11,000) run through liver sashimi, shirayaki, skewers, salad and an eel rice bowl. Diners praise attentive staff. Book dinner; it fills. Closes when the eel sells out.

osaka_chuka_soba_shinzans_honmachi.notes: [Ramen · kombu-water tsukemen and flying-fish shoyu by Honmachi] A clean counter shop between Honmachi and Sakaisuji-Honmachi with a Japanese-restaurant front, open since June 2026. The hit is the kombu-water tsukemen (¥920): glossy noodles sitting in kombu water, eaten first on their own with a pinch of sea or seaweed salt, then dipped in a sharp soy-based sauce, with the kombu water poured into the dip at the end. The shoyu soba is a light but deep seafood broth fragrant with grilled flying fish, and the shio soba is a clear broth with hand-kneaded curly noodles. House noodles are high-hydration and chewy. The special adds plump shrimp and meat wontons, rare shoulder chashu and a soft egg. There's also a hand-kneaded abura soba. Buy a ticket outside. Weekdays only; cash only.

osaka_onomichi_chuka_soba_daifuku_ueshio.notes: [Ramen · Onomichi back-fat shoyu with free rice refills near Tanimachi 6-chome] A bright, clean 13-seat counter on a back street south of Tanimachi 6-chome, open since November 2025 and bringing the rarely seen Onomichi style to Osaka. The chuka soba is a chicken-bone shoyu with a bold, slightly tart soy edge, scattered with pork back fat and served so hot that staff warn you; noodles are firm and medium-thin, with thin, tender chashu and menma. The deal is the ¥1,000 set, which adds free rice refills and a raw or seasoned egg: put the egg on rice, splash on some broth, or try the house tip of ao-gappa pickles with mayo. Gyoza are better than expected. Staff are cheerful, and you leave with a topping coupon. Lunch can stay nearly full until 13:30. Closed Thursdays; Wednesday lunch only.

Courses come with all-you-can-drink. The counter is free; tables cost ¥220 a person. Good for a quick first or second stop.

At lunch it's a Hakata tonkotsu shop: the ramen (¥900) looks rich but tastes clean and free of pork-bone funk, with a good balance of salt and fat and sizable, slightly sweet chashu, and the ramen with half fried rice (¥1,250) is a heavy lunch. There's also a black ramen and a tonkotsu miso. At night it turns into an izakaya with motsunabe, vinegared pork intestines, small gyoza and a fairly priced drinks list, handy for ramen with a drink. The counter can be packed at noon, but staff greet you cheerfully and cook with care. Closed Sundays.

osaka_muteppou_osaka_ebisuhoncho.notes: [Ramen · Osaka's famously thick tonkotsu by Imamiya-Ebisu] A pilgrimage bowl for tonkotsu lovers near Imamiya-Ebisu, open since 2005 and on Tabelog's ramen 100 lists most years since 2019. The broth is extraordinarily thick, slightly gritty and concentrated, like a pork-bone stew, yet not overly salty; it clings to thin curly noodles. Buy a ticket, then tell staff your noodle firmness, broth richness and green-onion amount. One regular always orders the chashu ramen, loaded with tender chashu, and recommends the thick spare ribs; get rice too. Change it up with garlic soy, pickled ginger and spicy takana from the table. Opinions in October 2026 were mixed: most still rave, but one long-time fan found the soup lukewarm and changed, and another found the noodles soft. There can be a line at opening. Cash only; closed Mondays.

chef_bio.background: Tonkotsu ramen shop (official site muteppou.com); Tabelog Ramen WEST 100 2019–2021, OSAKA 100 2023–2025.

anecdotes.text: "The broth is incredibly thick! Despite its richness, it's not overly salty, and the umami of the pork bone is concentrated, giving it a flavor reminiscent of a pork bone stew." — October 2026.
"The tonkotsu broth here is truly on another level. The thick, slightly gritty soup is delicious." — September 2026, chashu ramen.

osaka_ramen_kuon_senba.notes: [Ramen · a Tabelog 100 clear shio in the Senba Center Building basement] An eight-seat counter at the bottom of the escalator in Senba Center Building No. 3, directly connected to Sakaisuji-Hommachi, open since 2020 and on Tabelog's Ramen OSAKA 100 in 2024 and 2025. The shio ramen is the reason to come: a shimmering clear broth with a subtle yuzu aroma, light but deep, with house-made hand-pulled, aged high-hydration thin noodles that keep a firm, wheaty bite despite a very short boil. The special (¥1,680) carries chicken breast, chicken thigh and pork belly chashu and aosa seaweed; the seasoned-egg shio is ¥1,370. Save some broth for the yuzu ochazuke with shredded chashu. House rules: one bowl each, photos of food only, quiet please. Lunch only, until the soup runs out; check Instagram before going.

osaka_honmachi_seimensho_chuka_soba_kobo.notes: [Ramen · a house-noodle clear shoyu with a Sichuan-pepper lift in Senba] The chuka soba workshop of Honmachi Seimensho, now in the basement of Senba Center Building No. 2 right by the Sakaisuji-Hommachi gates, open since 2020 and often crowded at lunch. The chuka soba (¥1,050) is a clear shoyu with a citrus aroma and an elegant hint of Sichuan pepper, clean and deep, with no harsh heat; the Prime adds rare chashu and a seasoned egg. You choose flat or round house-made noodles, both chewy and wheaty. The dry chuka soba with egg and sudachi is the rich option, and in early October there was a chilled kiwi ramen (¥1,300). Self-serve rooibos tea. It often closes early when the noodles sell out, so go before late afternoon. Cash only; closed Sundays.

osaka_chuka_soba_fujii_ashiharabashi.notes: [Ramen · the original Fujii back-fat chuka soba by Ashiharabashi] The main shop of Chuka Soba Fujii, a minute from JR Ashiharabashi, open since 2011 and busy all day; the Namba branch is also in this guide. The chuka soba is a nostalgic clear shoyu of chicken bones with seafood and a hint of shiitake, deepened by back fat and paired with medium-thin straight noodles; set the firmness, richness and back fat, and extra green onion is free. The soy is on the strong side and the normal broth is rich, so one diner would go light next time. Sets are the draw: the ¥1,100 lunch set adds half fried rice and two crisp kara-age, and there's a nira soba buried in garlic chives with an egg yolk. Take a number from the machine inside and wait by phone; on a Sunday afternoon one diner was 20 groups back. Open until midnight, 01:30 on weekends; closed Thursdays.

chef_bio.background: Main shop of Chuka Soba Fujii (official site ra-men.co; Tabelog, staff-maintained).

anecdotes.text: "The clear soy sauce broth was rich with the umami of chicken bones, complemented by seafood flavors and the depth of back fat, creating a nostalgic yet satisfying taste. It paired perfectly with the medium-thin straight noodles." — October 2026, lunch set.

"I could choose the firmness of the noodles, the richness of the broth (normal or light), and the amount of back fat… Taking a sip of the broth, I could taste the soy sauce along with a hint of shiitake mushrooms." — October 2026.

osaka_shunsai_kaga_nishishinsaibashi.notes: [Japanese · a one-person obanzai counter tucked above Dotonbori] A hideaway on the fourth floor of a building just west of Midosuji, run single-handedly by a chatty, warm owner. There are eight seats at a sunken kotatsu-style counter facing the kitchen and one table, so it suits solo diners and couples. The cooking is homey seasonal Japanese: an assortment of six obanzai with a drink, sashimi you can build from three of the day's fish, light, crisp tempura (young corn in its husk, sweet potato that tastes stone-baked), braised chicken wings, sweet simmered herring and bamboo shoots in dashi. One regular comes two or three times a month, and the owner will adjust dishes to requests. One diner found the prices very reasonable. Lunch and dinner; closed Thursdays.

osaka_yakitori_kibitaki_bettei_shinsaiba.notes: [Yakitori · a dim, bar-like yakitori counter on Shinsaibashi-suji] The second room of Yakitori Kibitaki, one floor below the main shop, open since December 2023: 11 counter seats in a dark, stylish space more like a bar than a yakitori joint. Skewers are big, and the signatures seseri (neck) and negima come full size; take the omakase seven (¥2,800) or five, salt or tare, and look for chochin, heart and quail. Chicken here is served very fresh, with a sashimi platter (¥1,800), liver sashimi and tataki. There's a ¥500 seat charge, and dinner can be a timed seating when the next booking follows. Many guests are from overseas. Book on the official site; when the main shop is full, guests are sent here.

osaka_kasumaru_kasu_udon_higashishinsaib.notes: [Udon · all-night kasu udon, the Minami way to end a night out] A yatai-style udon shop in Higashi-Shinsaibashi, open since 2018, that runs from evening to the next morning, until 09:00 most days. The thing to order is kasu udon: chewy, medium-weight udon in a gently sweet, savory dashi topped with kasu, the crisp-fried beef offal that turns rich and juicy in the broth. Add meat, or go for the kasu curry udon with a raw egg (¥1,250) to mellow it. The oden (egg, daikon) is well soaked and tempts you into another drink; one diner found the kara-age soggy. One diner came to close a company party. Cards and QR accepted; Uber Eats too.

chef_bio.background: Kasu udon shop (Tabelog, staff-maintained).

anecdotes.text: "I love the texture of the kasu here; it's so rich and juicy. The udon has a great chewiness and the broth is delicious. The oden is infused with flavor." — December 2024, kasu udon (large) and oden.
"I ordered the meat kasu udon, so I got to enjoy both the meat and the kasu… The broth was reliably sweet, and I finished every drop!" — September 2026.

osaka_trebon_amemura.notes: [Okonomiyaki · a long-running Amemura teppan bar loved by regulars] A ten-seat counter around the teppan in Amerikamura, busy with locals from opening and hard to get into: one diner made it in on two of five tries. Start with the chicken heart (¥500), the house specialty, juicy with a 'magic' seasoning, then work through the vegetable list that regulars swear by: grilled lettuce, crisp Moroccan green beans, teppan konnyaku with ponzu. The tonpei-yaki, pork tamagoyaki and negi modan-yaki (¥1,400) are the heartier choices, and the yakisoba comes the classic way with aonori and pickled ginger. The cook is friendly. Sauce smoke clings to clothes, so dress casually. Cash only; generally no reservations, so call first.

chef_bio.background: Long-established teppan and okonomiyaki counter in Amerikamura (2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The first must-try dish at Trebon is the Chicken Heart (Hatsu). It's incredibly juicy, and the seasoning is just perfect!… The second dish you absolutely have to try is the Moroccan Green Beans." — September 2026.

"The yakisoba is served in the classic style, topped generously with aonori (seaweed) and beni shoga (pickled ginger). The grilled meat, piled high with green onions, was seasoned perfectly." — June 2026.

osaka_aioi_mochi_sennichimae.notes: [Japanese sweets · a 1961 night-only mochi shop off Dotonbori] A long-established mochi shop on the Aioibashi street near Hozenji, founded in 1961 and relocated nearby, that opens only in the evening and stays open until 01:30, made for a sweet stop after drinking. Get the grilled mochi (¥200) hot from the grill: white or yomogi, charred, stretchy and filled with red-bean paste, best eaten on the spot (one diner's takeaway stuck to the bag). There's also warabi mochi (¥350), ohagi five for ¥900 in kinako and smooth or chunky anko, and shiso mochi. Mochi is made without additives, so it doesn't keep; vacuum packs are available for souvenirs. The owner is friendly. PayPay accepted; closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Traditional mochi shop (Tabelog; 2025–2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "It has a wonderful yomogi aroma and is served hot and delicious. I also purchased a set of 5 Ohagi for JPY 900. You can choose your favorite combination from kinako, smooth red bean paste, and chunky red bean paste." — November 2025.

"With a nice char, this mochi is truly delicious! The chewy texture combined with the aroma of the char and the sweetness of the red bean paste creates a delightful experience!" — July 2026, grilled mochi ¥200.
