osaka_men_futari_uehommachi.notes: [Ramen · niboshi and clam shio by two people at Uehommachi] A fresh, stylish little shop a minute from Osaka-Uehommachi, open since September 2025 and run by two, the owner and one staff member per a regular. The broths are the point: niboshi shio or shoyu (¥1,200) with the sardine umami balanced, never overwhelming, and the shoyu showing a slight acidity; a sea bream and clam shio (¥1,450); and a limited shio tsukemen (¥1,350) whose dip blends clear chicken, seafood and domestic clam broth, with smooth house-made flat noodles of Haruyutaka wheat worth tasting with just salt first. Rare chashu turns tender in the hot broth. Add the sesame-scented sea bream rice. One regular reports a bronze at the Ramen Walker Grand Prix Kansai 2026. No table condiments; pay after. One October diner found service slow and the tsukemen noodles stuck together. Closed Tuesdays.

chef_bio.background: Ramen shop run by the owner and one staff member (October 2026 review).

anecdotes.text: "The Shio Tsukemen features firm, smooth, flat, medium-thick straight noodles paired with a dipping sauce made from a blend of chicken clear broth, seafood stock, and domestic clam broth." — October 2026, shio tsukemen large ¥1,450.
"The umami of the niboshi (dried sardines) was prominent, and the balance with the saltiness was exquisite. However, the niboshi flavor wasn't overwhelming." — October 2026, niboshi shio ramen.

osaka_men_no_ya_uehommachi.notes: [Ramen · a 2002 Uehommachi shop with house noodles and seasonal shio bowls] A neighborhood ramen shop a few minutes from Osaka-Uehommachi, open since 2002 and making its own noodles since 2006, with regulars logging dozens of visits. The everyday bowl is the original ramen (¥1,050), a light, refreshing shoyu with moist chashu and spinach, gentle on the body; the Manpuku set (+¥480) adds gyoza, kara-age and rice. The real draw is the rotating limited menu, with careful sourcing: chilled chicken shio topped with thick Hida tomato and Tokushima sudachi (¥1,500), a cold "adult" aemen with shiso, myoga and Senshu water eggplant, a Banshu Hyakujitsu chicken shio with chicken ham, curry tsukemen. Smooth, glossy house noodles; one seasonal bowl cost the same in any size. Add ginger or Sichuan-pepper oil. On one rainy Sunday, families lined up soon after opening. Closed Tuesdays.

chef_bio.background: Neighborhood ramen shop (Tabelog; Facebook page).

anecdotes.text: "The clear broth is paired with glossy noodles, topped with thick slices of Hida tomatoes and Tokushima sudachi… The homemade noodles glide smoothly down the throat, with a satisfying bounce when bitten into." — September 2026, chilled chicken shio with tomato and sudachi (large) ¥1,500.
"I ordered the Men no Ya Ramen Original Flavor for JPY 1,050, which has a light and refreshing soy sauce taste… The broth was truly refreshing, and the noodles were smooth and chewy." — October 2026.

osaka_men_shokudo_kohakudori_honmachi.notes: [Ramen · shijimi-clam shio and chicken soba by Honmachi] A small nine-seat shop two minutes from Honmachi, open since 2023 and, per one diner, from the same group as Subarushinbashi in Sakaisuji-Honmachi. The signature is the shio shijimi ramen (¥880): a light, clear broth with strong shijimi-clam umami and a perilla-leaf accent on medium-thick curly noodles; one diner found it a little sweet and samey by the end. The chicken soba is the other side, jidori chicken deepening with each sip under a sharp soy, on thin straight noodles with low-temperature chashu. Chashu is generous everywhere, especially in the abura soba, which comes with a small rice. Add the grilled diced chashu rice bowl. Open until 23:00; bowls are made with care, so allow ten minutes. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Ramen shop (Tabelog, staff-maintained); same group as Subarushinbashi, per a December 2025 review.

anecdotes.text: "After taking a sip of the broth, a strong umami flavor based on shijimi clams flooded my palate. The medium-thick curly noodles paired perfectly with the broth." — October 2026, shio shijimi ramen ¥880.

osaka_kitakata_shokudo_haihai_town.notes: [Ramen · Kitakata curly-noodle ramen with tuna rice bowls at Uehommachi] One of the few places in Osaka for Kitakata-style ramen, on the ground floor of Haihai Town by Osaka-Uehommachi Station, open since 2020. The kura-dashi shoyu comes light or rich: the rich version floats back fat but still drinks light, with the classic curly, high-hydration Kitakata noodles and chashu. There's a miso too. The house pairing is ramen with a tuna rice bowl from the counter's tuna display, toro-taku or negitoro yukke (¥1,350 as a set; one diner wanted more negitoro); a sign suggests eating the cold bowl first. Seasonal bowls rotate: harihari ramen with pork belly, mizuna and yuzu in autumn and winter, chilled tantanmen in summer. Open daily 11:00–22:00.

chef_bio.background: Kitakata ramen shop (Tabelog, staff-maintained).
chef_bio.specialty: Kitakata ramen with tuna rice bowls.

anecdotes.text: "The soy sauce broth was rich with a generous amount of back fat floating on top, but thanks to the mizuna and seasonings, it didn't feel heavy… The noodles were the characteristic curly, high-hydration type found in Kitakata ramen." — October 2026, harihari ramen.
"The broth is light despite being packed with back fat, and I love the curly noodles and the chashu." — October 2026, shoyu ramen (rich).

osaka_onomichi_ramen_juurokuban_shinmach.notes: [Ramen · a long-running Onomichi ramen counter by Nishinagahori] A small, traditional ten-seat counter near Nishinagahori, described by diners as a pioneer of Onomichi ramen in Osaka, with regulars lingering over gyoza and beer at night and a quick-turning line at lunch. The Juuroku Ban ramen is a nostalgic shoyu of Rausu kombu dashi and seafood with a layer of back fat, slightly sweet and easy to drink, on thin flat noodles brought from the Sebe noodle shop in Onomichi. Unusually for the style, it's meaty: thin lean chashu plus a tender, sweet-fatted kakuni of Wamochi pork, which one diner liked best with rice. Rice-and-kimchi sets run about ¥1,280, and the slightly large gyoza carry a hint of garlic. One diner found the bowl just average. Closed Sundays.

chef_bio.background: Long-established Onomichi ramen shop (Tabelog, staff-maintained; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The broth is a blend of Rausu kombu kelp dashi, seafood stock, and soy sauce, with added back fat for extra sweetness. The noodles are also noteworthy… flat noodles sourced daily from the long-established Sebe noodle shop in Onomichi." — October 2026, Juuroku ramen ¥990.

"The broth was light yet flavorful, with a strong bonito dashi and soy sauce taste. The back fat was not too overpowering. The noodles were thin and had a nice chewiness." — September 2026, Juuroku Ban ramen ¥1,150.

osaka_tsukemen_yondaime_misawa_honmachi.notes: [Ramen · pork-head and seafood double-soup tsukemen by Honmachi] A spacious tsukemen shop a minute from Honmachi, open since 2014 in a district crowded with ramen shops, from a tsukemen brand with other branches. The dip is a "double soup" of pork head and seafood, rich with fish powder and onion yet not heavy on the finish, clinging to thick, chewy, wheaty noodles; a hot stone rewarms it at the end. Toppings range from seasoned egg and chashu to niboshi, sudachi and umeboshi, and in summer there was an umeboshi tsukemen (¥1,100) with lime that even skeptics liked. For a bowl, the seafood tonkotsu ramen (¥950) has a powerful fish aroma. Open late on weekdays and Saturdays, all year; delivery via Uber Eats. Cash only.

chef_bio.background: Branch of the Tsukemen Misawa brand (official site smile-c.co.jp; Tabelog, staff-maintained).
chef_bio.philosophy: Pork-head and seafood double soup; hot stone to keep the dip warm (official site).

anecdotes.text: "You can really taste the umami from the seafood, and despite its richness, the aftertaste isn't too heavy, making it easy to keep eating. The noodles have a great texture." — August 2026, tsukemen.
"The chewy noodles had a strong wheat flavor and were deliciously thick… the plum adds a fantastic twist, with its acidity refreshing on a hot summer day." — July 2026, umeboshi tsukemen ¥1,100.

osaka_menya_buttoku_ikero_minamihonmachi.notes: [Ramen · the thickest noodles around, in mazesoba, by Honmachi] A basement shop a minute from Honmachi, open since 2022 (formerly Shogun Mazesoba, per one diner), built around extra-thick, curly domestic-wheat noodles it bills as among Kansai's thickest. The Buttoku mazesoba (¥980) is the order: wide, chewy noodles with diced chashu, green onion and egg yolk in a rich, junky sauce; mix hard, then change it up with aged vinegar, chili oil and garlic from the table, and finish with rice and broth as chazuke. There's a thick ramen (¥1,080) too. On the 22nd of each month, Buttoku Day, the mazesoba drops to ¥500, and one regular never misses it. Busy at weekend lunch. Weekday dinners until 23:00.

chef_bio.origin: Opened 24 October 2022 (Tabelog); formerly Shogun Mazesoba (October 2026 review).
chef_bio.background: Thick-noodle mazesoba shop (official site buttokuikiro.com; Tabelog, staff-maintained).

anecdotes.text: "The thick noodles are incredibly satisfying, paired with diced chashu and green onions… The recommended way to enjoy it is to mix everything vigorously, incorporate the raw egg, and then enhance the flavor with the table condiments: aged vinegar, chili oil, and garlic sauce." — October 2026, Buttoku mazesoba ¥980.
"I ordered my monthly favorite, the 'Buttoku Mazesoba' for JPY 500, and of course, I added the Large Size for JPY 150." — September 2026, Buttoku Day.

osaka_menya_kyubee_minamihonmachi.notes: [Ramen · chicken-oil shoyu and a Friday izakaya near Sakaisuji-Honmachi] A clean, stylish ramen shop two minutes from Sakaisuji-Honmachi, open since 2021. The chuka soba is a rich shoyu glossy with chicken oil, on medium-thick, firm, chewy noodles with rare chashu; one diner drank every drop. In summer there was a chilled soba of kombu and bonito dashi topped with kumquat and minced chicken. Opinions on other bowls vary: one diner found the shio too oily and salty, another found the broth lukewarm at opening. Fridays it stays open to 20:00 and adds an izakaya menu from 15:00, with fresh chicken at bargain prices: toro liver and chicken sashimi ¥400 each, kara-age ¥150 for two, highballs ¥350. Weekdays only; cash only.

chef_bio.background: Ramen shop with a Friday izakaya menu (Tabelog, staff-maintained; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "The broth was rich with a generous amount of chicken oil and a delightful soy sauce aroma—it was incredibly delicious. I ended up drinking it all. The noodles were medium-thick with a chewy texture and had a strong bite." — September 2026, chuka soba with half fried rice set.

"Personally, I found that the umami of the kombu came through first, followed by a subtle hint of bonito… The firm, medium-thick noodles had a smooth texture and a nice chew." — September 2026, chilled soba with kumquat.

osaka_tempura_ando_soemoncho.hours_raw: Mon–Sat one seating at 18:00 (doors 17:45); Sun two seatings at 12:00 and 18:00 (doors 11:45 and 17:45); irregular holidays (Tabelog, staff-maintained). Course only, about ¥20,000–30,000. Cards, PayPay and WeChat Pay accepted (Tabelog). End times not listed.
osaka_tempura_ando_soemoncho.notes: [Japanese · a Tabelog 100 tempura counter frying in olive oil] A calm basement counter of hinoki wood just off the Soemoncho nightlife strip, open since 2021 and picked for Tabelog's Tempura 100 in 2025. The difference is the oil: extra-virgin olive oil at low temperature, which the shop says soaks in less and drains well, so even a long course stays light. The omakase opens with a surprise katsu sandwich, then runs through seasonal seafood and growers' vegetables: several kinds of shrimp including heads and roe, young ayu, sea urchin, sweet carrots and sweet potato, plus Kagawa Olive Beef, and finishes with tencha. Diners describe the chef as friendly and talkative about the ingredients. About ten seasonal sakes. One seating nightly at 18:00, plus Sunday lunch; book ahead.

chef_bio.background: Tempura counter (official site tenpura-ando.com; Tabelog, staff-maintained); Tabelog Tempura 100 2025.
chef_bio.philosophy: Extra-virgin olive oil and low-temperature frying to keep the umami, sweetness and aroma of the ingredients (Tabelog listing).

anecdotes.text: "The tempura, fried in olive oil, has an astonishingly light batter that doesn't weigh you down at all. I was impressed by the precise cooking techniques used for each ingredient. The carrots and sweet potatoes were exceptionally delicious." — August 2026.
"The course starts with a surprising katsu sandwich, followed by a parade of delicious tempura." — September 2026.

osaka_yoshitaka_oden_higashishinsaibashi.gf_detail: Not gluten-free in practice: soy-seasoned oden broth, fried abura kasu, somen.
osaka_yoshitaka_oden_higashishinsaibashi.vegan_detail: Not vegan: dashi-based oden, seafood, beef tongue, chicken.
osaka_yoshitaka_oden_higashishinsaibashi.hours_raw: Tue–Sun 18:00–23:00; closed Mondays (Tabelog, staff-maintained). Reservations advised; hard to book in winter (June 2026). 10% service charge. Cards and PayPay accepted (Tabelog).
osaka_yoshitaka_oden_higashishinsaibashi.notes: [Japanese · refined oden and sake hidden in Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A quiet, old-Shinsaibashi-style oden counter at the very back of a building's second floor, open since 2014, with classical music playing. The oden is the heart of it, delicately seasoned: daikon, konnyaku, big clams with kuzukiri, green onion with abura kasu, tuna negima, whale saezuri and yuba. Around it come seasonal plates: an oden-broth soup with wild mushrooms and free-range chicken, a shime-saba sandwich, hairy crab packed in its shell, umazurahagi with its liver, a fluffy sardine tsukune that converted a sardine skeptic, crisp grilled eel. Good sake to match. Dinner runs about ¥10,000–20,000 with a 10% service charge, and one table waited a long time for dishes. Book ahead, especially in winter; closed Mondays.

chef_bio.background: Oden and Japanese restaurant (official site yoshitaka-osaka.jp; Tabelog, staff-maintained).

anecdotes.text: "First, we have the oden broth soup infused with the umami of natural mushrooms. One sip, and the rich flavor spreads pleasantly." — October 2026, seventh visit.
"From the oden, we enjoyed the Japanese radish, konnyaku (konjac), clams, and kuzukiri (starch noodles) which were all flavorful… The grilled eel was perfectly crispy on the outside." — May 2026.

osaka_nanchi_suehiro_zushi_sennichimae.notes: [Sushi · a century-old Minami sushi counter by Aioibashi] An eight-seat counter of pale wood near Aioibashi, a long-established sushi house that one diner dates back more than 100 years, which began with Kamigata (Osaka-style) sushi and now serves Edomae. Book the omakase of appetizers and 12 nigiri, or order à la carte; one diner found the prices reasonable. Highlights in reviews: crisp torigai, thick lightly grilled nodoguro, abalone with its liver sauce over rice, a refined anago, and sea urchin that melts away. Seasoning is balanced, neither too sweet nor too sour. Not every visit lands: one diner found some pieces fishy or too salty. Enter by 21:30; closed Sundays.

chef_bio.origin: Founded over 100 years ago, per a July 2026 review.

Cards accepted; no e-money or QR (Tabelog).
osaka_sushi_ichiei_sennichimae.notes: [Sushi · a young omakase counter with a sweet-shrimp signature in Sennichimae] A seven-seat hinoki counter in a basement off Sennichimae, open since October 2023, which one regular says has been a Michelin Guide Kyoto-Osaka selected restaurant in 2025 and 2026. The omakase (about ¥25,000) opens with clam soup and the signature: sweet shrimp spread paper-thin, eaten with rock salt and sudachi. Appetizers are inventive, such as eel and cucumber wrapped Peking-duck style, kue or kinmedai shabu-shabu, abalone with liver sauce, before nigiri of seasonal fish the chef sources directly from producers and Toyosu. The chef seems reserved at first but warms up; the host is friendly. Three seatings a day; book well ahead.

"The sushi ingredients are sourced directly by the chef, who visits the production areas and sometimes purchases from fishermen, as well as acquiring necessary ingredients from Toyosu Market." — September 2026.

osaka_junchan_zushi_sennichimae.notes: [Sushi · a busy, generous Minami sushi bar regulars rebook] A popular 19-seat sushi bar a block off Dotonbori, usually full, with regulars who book the same day and come back often. Portions are big: oversized toppings, huge rolls and sashimi platters piled with toro, kazunoko, scallops, flounder and geoduck. The favorite is the toro-taku roll (only one toro item per table, so choose between it and the toro tekka); aburi salmon, rare and juicy, comes close behind, with eel and anago. Start with the crab-claw sunomono in sweet vinegar or the kani miso, which pull you toward sake. There's no price list, but two diners paid about ¥17,000 with drinks. Popular items sell out; one diner found the rolls unevenly cut. Closed Mondays.

chef_bio.background: Sushi bar (Tabelog, staff-maintained; 2026 reviews).

anecdotes.text: "My favorites are toro-taku, aburi salmon, aburi scallops, and eel!… The aburi salmon is rare and incredibly juicy!" — September 2026, fifth visit.
"You can only order one item that has 'toro' in it… this time I went for toro tekka! It was packed with toro, and the portion was huge." — September 2026.

osaka_chuka_soba_fukuemon_uehommachi.notes: [Ramen · a homey shoyu chuka soba with sets by Uehommachi] A red-neon, graffiti-windowed ramen shop a minute from Osaka-Uehommachi, open since 2016, with the broad menu and sets of a neighborhood Chinese diner and a loyal crowd of regulars. The shoyu chuka soba is a chicken-and-seafood broth with a strong, nostalgic soy edge, gentle rather than salty, on medium-thin low-hydration noodles with three slices of chashu, menma, sprouts and green onion; at lunch, extra sprouts and onion are free. For more richness there's a back-fat version. Sets add gyoza or a small soy-dark fried rice (¥1,200 with gyoza), and evenings bring a beer set with fatty chashu. Grated garlic is on the table. Service is attentive. Closed Sundays.

"The broth had a strong soy sauce flavor, reminiscent of chicken and pork-based soups you might find in Kyoto, which felt nostalgic to me. The noodles were medium-thin and straight." — September 2026, shoyu ramen and gyoza set.

osaka_menya_rapasu_minamihonmachi.notes: [Ramen · clam paitan "Rapasu", ramen meets pasta, by Sakaisuji-Honmachi] A stylish little shop near Sakaisuji-Honmachi, open since 2024 and popular on social media, that crosses ramen with pasta. The Asari Rapasu (¥1,230; the SP version ¥1,580) is a mild, Western-leaning broth of clam dashi and chicken paitan on flat, wide, chewy noodles, with chashu, tender chicken, clams, yuzu and a squeeze of lemon; diners compare it to a Western-style mazesoba. The original ramen is a creamy but light chicken paitan with spinach, minced onion and rare chashu. Finish with tomato-cheese rice. One diner found the concept more fun than memorable. Order by QR code; the owner and staff are friendly and happy to explain the menu.

osaka_machida_shoten_honmachi.notes: [Ramen · a reliable Yokohama iekei chain bowl by Honmachi, to midnight] The Honmachi shop of the Machida Shoten iekei chain, a minute from Honmachi exit 9, open since 2023 and lined up at lunch. The ramen (¥880) is a punchy tonkotsu-shoyu with thick noodles, spinach, nori and chashu; set your firmness, richness and fat when you order, and note the regular is salty for some. The value draw: rice is free until 18:00, and one regular dips the nori in the soup and wraps the rice with the counter's pickles, onions and ginger. App members at Gold rank get toppings free. Consistent rather than surprising, which one regular sees as the point. Open daily until midnight; transit IC cards only, no credit cards.

osaka_butakin_uehommachi.notes: [Ramen · a beginner-friendly Jiro-style bowl by Uehommachi] A Jiro-style shop two minutes from Osaka-Uehommachi, open since February 2025, with a relaxed atmosphere that diners call easy for first-timers. Sizes start big: the small is 250 g of thick, chewy, wheaty noodles (¥1,100), the large 375 g (¥1,200), the extra-large 500 g. Buy a ticket, then call your garlic, vegetables and fat; vegetables run a bit light by Jiro standards unless you ask for more. The broth leans soy over pork, with a touch of sweetness, under thick pork, bean sprouts and cabbage. Garlic mayo (+¥100) and spicy fried garlic push it further into junk-food territory, and the back-fat rice bowl is a guilty side. One diner could not add garlic on a daytime visit. Busy at lunch; open daily.

osaka_kadoya_shokudo_sohonten_shinmachi.notes: [Ramen · Osaka's benchmark Nagoya Cochin shoyu and tsukesoba by Nishinagahori] The main shop of Kadoya Shokudo, open since 2001 and on Tabelog's ramen 100 every year since 2018, one of Osaka's most famous bowls (the Crysta Nagahori branch is also in this guide). Everything rests on Nagoya Cochin chicken. The tsukesoba (¥1,880 for 200 g) is the order to make: a dip of intense chicken umami with soy, a tang of vinegar and a little chili, with glossy, smooth house-made medium-thick noodles; the larger sizes add more to the dip. The shoyu chuka soba and the handmade wonton noodles (shio or shoyu) are the alternatives, and the Cochin seasoned egg is ¥350. On weekends there's a limited Cochin chicken rice. Lines run 30 minutes to two hours; the shop lends umbrellas for shade. Lunch only; closed Tuesday and Wednesday; cash only.

On one visit every later arrival ordered the kai soba, a light clam broth where the shellfish shines. Add a chashu rice bowl. Service is attentive and the room calm. The evening session opens at 19:00 Tuesday to Friday, and seven seats fill in one round. Check X for closures; closed Mondays; cash only.

The rich tsukemen (¥1,200) pairs house-made thick, chewy, slightly sweet wheat noodles with a dip so thick it clings, built on pork, chicken, sardine flakes and niboshi; order it soy or curry, the curry adding a gentle spice. Large noodles are free, but the dip is strong and a small rice comes at the end to mix with the leftover dip and yuzu kosho, so regular may be enough. Lemon halfway brightens it. The mazesoba (¥1,150) adds cheese, fried onion and garlic chives. One regular has eaten here twenty times. Buy a ticket outside; open daily; cash only.

osaka_katanami_maguro_nishishinsaibashi.notes: [Sushi · a showy tuna omakase counter just off Dotonbori] A six-seat counter on a third floor near Namba, calm despite the crowds below, built around tuna and theatre. The omakase (¥12,000 in October 2026) opens with a bowl heaped with uni, ikura and otoro that the chef sears in front of you, then the "Dragon Roll" of otoro, negitoro, uni and egg yolk, and a tuna flight of akami, chutoro and otoro. Shira-ko with ponzu, a gold-leaf uni tofu, nigiri of shrimp, sea bream, scallop and salmon, and an unagi dog handed straight across the counter round it out. Reviews call it visually spectacular and, past the show, well made. Open from noon, so it works for a splurge lunch too. Book ahead.

"While the initial impression was the vibrant presentation, I was pleased to find that the quality of the ingredients was excellent, and every dish was delicious." — October 2026, omakase ¥12,000.

osaka_sushi_hibiki_soemoncho.notes: [Sushi · a lively ¥4,400 omakase in two seatings on Soemoncho] A counter sushi bar from the 881 ("Yabai") Group, open since June 2025, whose idea is authentic counter sushi made approachable and fun. There's one omakase (¥4,400), or ¥6,600 with all-you-can-drink, served to eight guests at a time in two seatings at 17:30 and 20:00, opening with a group shout-out. The course runs about 15 items: Tosa katsuo, chawanmushi, seasonal fish sandwiches, kamasu, yuan-yaki, tuna, unadon, then chanko and a ramen made from the broth of the sushi fish. Diners love the warm, playful atmosphere and the head chef's friendliness; one found only six nigiri and no chutoro, and the shaved-ice dessert plain. The door shows only a QR sign. Reservation only.

osaka_chuka_stand_pyu_higashishinsaibash.notes: [Chinese · a late-night gyoza counter open until 3 am in Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A casual counter Chinese bar, open since 2022, made for a second or third stop: it runs until 03:00 most nights. osaka_kagome_curry_udon_higashishinsaiba.notes: [Udon · thin-noodle curry udon, the Minami night-out finish] A small, glass-fronted counter just north of Aioibashi, run by two people, where diners end a night of drinking with curry udon. The curry is light and rich in dashi, with noticeably good beef, and it comes over very thin noodles that slip down easily, unusual for curry udon (¥1,100; kizami with fried tofu ¥1,200; tempura too). Add kayaku gohan (¥350). For something gentler, there's a sudachi udon fragrant with citrus, a warm nyumen with fluffy egg, or plain kizami udon. On one weekday evening it was busy with families and regulars, and more overseas visitors have found it lately. Open 18:00 to 01:30; closed Sundays; cash only.

osaka_kan_izakaya_higashishinsaibashi.notes: [Japanese · a creative seafood-and-meat izakaya in Higashi-Shinsaibashi] A tucked-away izakaya in the middle of the Minami nightlife streets, open since 2015, with a counter downstairs and a second-floor room that groups of about ten can book. The menu runs from seafood to meat and seasonal plates: bluefin tuna and yellowtail-belly sashimi, shirako with ponzu, scallop butter that left one table speechless, fried oysters, sanma and matsutake in foil, a beef cutlet and uni cream pasta, but the dish people come back for is the shrimp mayo. The sake list is broad. There are no prices on the menu and portions scale to your group, so ask; dinners ran about ¥5,000–15,000. One diner found service slow and the room noisy, another found it calm and suited to business dinners. Book ahead; closed Sundays.

osaka_fukuryu_ramen_wadachi_honmachi.notes: [Ramen · the foam-whipped chicken paitan of Honmachi] The main shop of Wadachi, a minute or two from Honmachi's Yotsubashi-line exits, open since 2014 and a Tabelog ramen 100 regular from 2017 to 2023. Its signature Fuku Ryu ramen (¥930) is a chicken paitan shoyu whipped into a creamy, cappuccino-like foam, topped with rare chashu, green onion, mizuna and a slightly tangy foam that blends in as you go; thin straight noodles stay firm. Portions are modest, so add the kara-age and rice set. One regular prefers the niboshi shoyu with onions and thick chashu, lighter than it looks; others order the Mazenibou niboshi mazesoba, best with vinegar and a few pieces of meat saved for the rice. Fills by noon on weekdays. Open daily; bring cash.

"The finely whipped broth resembles a cappuccino, providing a unique twist compared to typical ramen." — October 2026.

osaka_chuka_soba_subaru_honmachibashi.notes: [Ramen · additive-free whole-chicken chuka soba near Sakaisuji-Honmachi] A clean shop five minutes from Sakaisuji-Honmachi, open since 2022 and committed to no additives or chemical seasonings. The marudori (whole-chicken) chuka soba looks dark but drinks light and refreshing, with medium-thin noodles, rare chashu and tender menma; the special (¥1,300) adds a well-seasoned egg. The shio comes with a dab of wasabi to stir in midway, and there's a niboshi mazesoba with a strong sardine note. In season, a chilled abura soba (¥1,050) with chashu, egg yolk and fish powder is good with plenty of vinegar. The rare chashu rice bowl is a strong lunch side, and lunch sets are ¥100 off. One diner found the soup lukewarm and wanted more depth. Pay on the way out; cash only.

osaka_men_no_kamino_ebisunishi.notes: [Ramen · a ¥750 shoyu with mitsuba, and ¥500 morning ramen, by Ebisucho] A ten-seat counter a few minutes from Ebisucho, open since 2021 and loved for good ramen at a low price. The shoyu ramen (¥750) is a seafood dashi deepened with chicken bones and chicken fat, easy to drink, on thin but chewy noodles, with thin chashu and an unexpected sprig of mitsuba; there's a shio too. Early risers can get a plain morning ramen for ¥500, a clear, dashi-rich bowl that soothes a hangover. On rainy days extra noodles are free. Add a ¥300 chashu rice bowl or the limited meat-and-egg bowl. Staff service is warm. Hours seem to vary, so check before an evening visit; closed Mondays; cash only.

osaka_jonetsu_no_buta_awaza.notes: [Ramen · seafood tonkotsu and rich tsukemen by Awaza] A lively counter shop a minute or two from Awaza, open since 2023 and packed even on a rainy weekday evening. The seafood tonkotsu ramen (¥970) is rich and creamy, with medium-thick straight noodles, chashu, a seasoned egg, wood-ear mushroom, nori and plenty of green onion in a striking round bowl. The rich tsukemen (¥1,050) has a strong pork-bone dip, and the mazesoba, with a different kind of punch, comes with white rice; pair a bowl with the meat-and-egg-yolk rice bowl on hungry days. Summer brought a chilled chuka soba with pork soft-bone chashu. The owner and staff keep the mood bright. One diner found the tsukemen just average. Buy a ticket first; closed Mondays; cash only.
